उसका उचित रूप से निपटान किया गया; 


और सक्षम प्राधिकारी ने उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 3घ की उपधारा (॥) के अनुसरण में, केन्द्रीय सरकार को अपनी 
रिपोर्ट दे दी है;

उचित रूप से निपटान किया गया;

प्रयोजन के लिए अर्जन किया जाना चाहिए ;

the same appropriately; 


And whereas, in pursuance of sub-section (l) of section 3D of the said Act, the competent authority has 
submitted its report to the Central Government; 


Now, therefore, upon receipt of the said report of the competent authority and in exercise of the powers 
conferred by the sub-section (l) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government hereby declares that the land 
specified in the said Schedule should be acquired for the aforesaid purpose;

Recruitment Regulations, 2014, except as respects things done or omitted to be done before such supersession, the 
Employees’ State Insurance Corporation hereby makes with the approval of the Central Government the following 
regulations, regulating the method of recruitment to the post of Deputy Director in the Employees’ State Insurance 
Corporation, namely:- 


1. Short title and commencement. - (1) These regulations may be called the Employees’ State Insurance Corporation, 
Deputy Director, Recruitment Regulations, 2026. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 


2. Number of posts, classification, level in Pay Matrix.- The number of post, its classification, level in the pay matrix 
attached thereto, shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of the Schedule annexed to these regulations. 


3. Method of recruitment, age- limit, qualifications, etc. - The method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications and 
other matters relating to the said post shall be as specified in columns (5) to (13) of the said Schedule. 


4. Disqualification. - No person- 


(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or 


(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person,shall be eligible for 
appointment to the said post: 


Provided that the Chairman of the Employees’ State Insurance Corporation may, if satisfied that such marriage 
is permissible under the personal law applicable to such person and to the other party to the marriage and that there are 
other grounds for so doing, exempt such person from the operation of this regulation.

is necessary or expedient so to do, he may, with the approval of the Chairman of the Employees’ State Insurance 
Corporation, after taking prior approval of the Central Government and in consultation with the Union Public Service 
Commission, by order and for reasons to be recorded in writing, relax any of the provisions of these regulations, with 
respect to any class or category of persons. 


6. Savings. - Nothing in these regulations shall affect the reservation, relaxation of age-limit and other concessions 
required to be provided for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, other backward classes, ex-Servicemen and 
other special categories of persons in accordance with the orders issued by the Central Government from time to time, 
in this regard.

BUREAU OF INDIAN STANDARDS 
(Department of Consumer Affairs) 
NOTIFICATION 

New Delhi, the 4th November, 2026 
F. No. BS/XI/09/02/2026-27.— In exercise of the powers conferred by section 39 of the Bureau of Indian 
Standards Act, 2016 (11 of 2016) and in supersession of the Bureau of Indian Standards (Recruitment to Laboratory 
Technical Posts) Regulations, 2019, except as respects things done or omitted to be done before such supersession, the 
Bureau, with the previous approval of the Central Government hereby makes the following regulations regulating the 


method of recruitment to the posts of Laboratory Technical in the Bureau of Indian Standards, Ministry of Consumer 
Affairs, namely:— 


1. Short Title and Commencement. -- (1). These regulations may be called the Bureau of Indian Standards 
(Recruitment to Laboratory Technical Posts) Regulations, 2026. 

(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 

2s Definitions. — (1) In these regulations, unless the context otherwise requires - 

(a) “Act” means the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 (11 of 2016); 

(b) “appointing authority”, means the Deputy Director General (Administration); 

(c) “employee” means the employee appointed on regular basis in the Bureau of Indian Standards and 
includes the employee of the erstwhile Indian Standards Institution; 

(d) “Laboratory Technical Posts” means the posts specified in column (2) of the First Schedule; 

(e) “officiating appointment” means appointing an officer already holding a post in a substantive or 
officiating capacity to officiate, as a temporary measure, in one or more of other independent posts 
at a time; 

(f) “Public Disclosure Scheme” means the initiative of the Department of Personnel and Training, 


Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievance and Pensioners, Government of India wherein for making 
available publicly scores of non-recommended willing candidates (Candidates who qualify the

conducted by the Central Government recruiting agencies viz. Union Public Service Commission,

Selection Commission, etc.; 


(g) “rules” means the Bureau of Indian Standards Rules, 2018; 
(h) “Schedule” means a Schedule appended to these regulations; 
(1) “Selection Committee” means the committee constituted under regulation 8; 
(2) Words and expressions used in here and not defined, but defined in the Act or the rules, shall have the same 


meaning as respectively assigned to them in the Act or the rules, as the case may be. 


3. Method of recruitment. — The method of recruitment, level in Pay Matrix, age-limit, qualifications and 
other matters connected thereto shall be as specified in columns (4) to (10) of the First Schedule. 


4. Procedure for making Direct Recruitment. — (1) Where any post specified in column (2) of the First 
Schedule is required to be filled by direct recruitment, the following procedure shall be followed, namely: — 


A. Order of priority for methods of recruitment. - Recruitment to posts shall be carried out in accordance with 
the following order of priority: - 


(i) 


First Priority - Public Disclosure Scheme. - First preference shall be given to filling posts through 


the Public Disclosure Scheme; 


(ii) 


Second Priority - Other Methods (Competitive examination or departmental recruitment): Second 


preference to be given to recruitment through open competitive examination as prescribed under clause (c) 
shall be resorted to only when the Public Disclosure Scheme is inapplicable or unavailable: 


Provided that, if vacancies remain unfilled through the Public Disclosure Scheme, the same may be 


filled through other methods (Competitive examination or departmental recruitment) specified as under: -

limit, qualifications and experience, as specified in the First Schedule and such other matter as may

at least fifty per cent marks in the aggregate. 


B. Selection through Public Disclosure Scheme — In case of posts to be filled through Public Disclosure 
Scheme, the procedure shall be as follows:- 


(a) 


(b) 


candidates shall be selected discipline wise or trade wise on the basis of the final score secured in 
the latest examination conducted under the Public Disclosure Scheme subject to their qualifying the 
skill test conducted by the Bureau; 


the examination under the Public Disclosure Scheme through which recruitment is to be made shall 
be approved by the Director General: 


Provided that the selection shall be made without any interview by the Bureau.

(०) where posts reserved for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, ex-Servicemen or other 
special categories of persons cannot filled on the basis of the criteria specified therein, the 
candidates belonging to such category may be selected by giving relaxation as per the Government 
guidelines, to make-up the deficiency in the reserved quota, subject to suitability of such candidates 
for selection to the post concerned; 


(2) a reserve list in addition to the select list of successful candidates shall be drawn up for filling up the 
vacancies which shall remain valid for a period of one year from the date when such list is drawn: 


Provided that the number of candidates in reserve list shall not exceed the number of posts advertised. 


(3) The candidates appointed by direct recruitment shall be on probation for a period of two years in accordance 
with the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards (Terms and Conditions of Service of Employees) Regulations, 
2020, during which period, they may be required to undergo such training or may be given such responsibilities as 
may be deemed necessary by the appointing authority or may be required to pass departmental examination or 
examinations for successful completion of probation: 


Provided that the module of the training, responsibilities to be given and the departmental examination to be 
passed for successful completion of probation shall be such as may be recommended by the appointing authority and 
approved by the Director General. 


5. Promotion. — (1) Where any posts specified in column (2) of the First Schedule is required to be filled by 
promotion, the promotion shall be made on the recommendation of the Selection Committee constituted by the 
Director General from amongst the employees in the lower grade on the basis of merit or with due regard to seniority. 


(2) The regular employees shall be entitled to the grant of financial up-gradation under the Modified Assured 
Career Progression Scheme as admissible to the employees of the Central Government. 


(3) Non-functional Grade I and Grade II shall be granted to Laboratory Officers as specified in the First 
Schedule. 


6. Deputation. — (1) Where any posts specified in column (2) of the First Schedule is required to be filled by 
deputation, such posts shall be advertised in at least two leading newspapers and also on the website of the Bureau and 
the administrative department of the Central Government having administrative control of the Bureau giving full 
information regarding number of posts, qualifications, experience, age-limit, special expertise, if any, as specified in 
the First Schedule and such other matters as may be necessary: 


Provided that the maximum age limit for appointment on deputation basis shall not be exceeding fifty-six 
years on the closing date of the receipt of the applications: 


Provided further that the period of deputation shall not ordinarily exceed three years and the maximum period 
of deputation shall be five years. 


(2) The candidates who fulfill the prescribed requirements and shortlisted by the Screening Committee 
constituted under regulation 7 shall be recommended for selection. 


7. Screening Committee for selection by direct recruitment or deputation. — (1) The Screening Committee 
shall consist of three officers of the Bureau not below the rank of Scientist ‘C’ to be nominated by the Director 
General and the senior-most amongst them shall be the Chairperson of the committee. 


(2) The candidates shortlisted by the Screening Committee shall be considered by the Selection Committee for 
selection. 
8. Selection Committee. - (1) The Selection Committee shall be constituted by the Director General as under: 
(1) the Selection Committee shall consist of the following members, namely :- 
(a) an officer not below the rank of Scientist ‘F’ or the Deputy Director General, who shall be the 
Chairperson; 
(b) the Director or Head or Officer in-charge of the Department dealing with the personnel functions in 
the Bureau; 
(c) two officers not below the rank of Scientist ‘C’ or the Deputy Director, of whom at least one shall 
be from the Scheduled Caste or the Scheduled Tribe; and 
(d) the Deputy Director or Assistant Director dealing with the personnel functions in the Bureau. 
(2) The recommendations made by the Selection Committee referred to in sub-regulation (1) shall be submitted 


to the Director General for approval.

9. Appointing Authority. - (1) The appointments shall be made by the appointing authority on the 
recommendations of the Selection Committee: 


Provided that the officiating appointments may be made by the appointing authority without 
recommendations of the Selection Committee subject to conditions specified for such appointments in the Schedule 
appended to the Bureau of Indian Standards (Powers and Duties of Director General) Regulations, 2018: 


Provided further that the respective Selection Committees shall also function as the Screening Committee for 
the purpose of considering and recommending the cases for grant of financial up-gradation under the Modified 
Assured Career Progression Scheme specified in sub-regulation (2) of regulation 5 and the Non-Functional Grade I 
and Grade II, as specified in sub-regulation (3) thereof. 


10. Categories of posts and sanctioned strength. - (1) The categories of posts and their sanctioned strength 
shall be such as may be determined by the Executive Committee from time to time, with the approval of the Central 
Government. 


(2) The categories of posts and their sanctioned strength as on the date of the notification of these regulations 
shall be such as specified in the First Schedule and the disciplines or trades of the posts shall be as specified in the 
Second Schedule. 


11. Power to relax. - Where the Bureau is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to do, it may, for 
reasons to be recorded in writing, relax any of the provisions of these regulations in respect of any class or category of 
persons with the approval of the Central Government. 


12. Savings. - Nothing in these regulations shall affect reservations, relaxation of age-limit and other concessions 
required to be provided for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, ex-Servicemen and other special categories of 
persons as specified by the Central Government from time to time. 


13. Interpretation. — If any question arises relating to the interpretation of these regulations, it shall be decided 
by the Bureau with the approval of the Central Government.

सड़कों और पुलों के लिए विनिर्दिष्ट भार प्रतिबंधों का अनुपालन किया जाएगा और यानों को सड़कों पर लाने से पहले, 
ऐसे प्राधिकारियों से अनुमति ली जाएगी। सुरक्षा की दृष्टि से ट्रैलरों का प्रत्येक प्रचालन राज्य/संघ राज्य क्षेत्र/भारतीय

रखी एगी। 


iii. ट्रांसपोर्टर इस तरह के प्रतिबंधों का पालन करेगा जैसा कि राज्य / संघ राज्य क्षेत्र सरकार / भारतीय राष्ट्रीय राजमार्ग 
प्राधिकरण /राष्ट्रीय राजमार्ग एवं अवसंरचना विकास निगम लिमिटेड इस संबंध में आदेश द्वारा निर्दिष्ट कर सकता Sl 


iv. ट्रांसपोर्टर, यानों को सड़कों पर लाने से पहले, किसी भी वस्तु जैसे होर्डिंग्स, GH, साइनबोर्ड को हटाने के लिए, 
ट्रांसमिशन लाइन बंद कराना इत्यादि के लिए, राज्य/संघ राज्य क्षेत्र सरकार के संबंधित विभागों से आवश्यक पूर्व 
अनुमति प्राप्त करेगा और इस तरह के प्रतिबंधों का पालन करेगा जैसा कि राज्य / संघ राज्य क्षेत्र / भारतीय राष्ट्रीय 
राजमार्ग प्राधिकरण/ राष्ट्रीय राजमार्ग एवं अवसंरचना विकास निगम लिमिटेड इस संबंध में आदेश द्वारा विनिर्दिष्ट 
करता है। राज्य/संघ राज्य क्षेत्र सरकार द्वारा अनुमत, किसी भी वस्तु को हटाने और पुनर्विकास कराने की लागत मैसर्स 
अलाइन ग्लोबल लॉजिस्टिक्स प्रा. लि. द्वारा वहन की जाएगी।

G.S.R. 975(E).— Whereas, in the matter of import of Alloy Steel Chisel/tool and Hydraulic Rock Breaker in 
fully assembled condition (hereinafter referred to as the subject goods), originating in or exported from China PR and 
Korea RP, the designated authority, vide its final findings notification F. No. 6/8/2022-DGTR, dated the 28th March, 
2024, had recommended imposition of anti-dumping duty on imports of the subject goods; 


And whereas, on the basis of the aforesaid findings of the designated authority, the Central Government had 
imposed anti-dumping duty on the subject goods vide notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of Finance 
(Department of Revenue), No. !/2024-Customs (ADD), dated the 27th June, 2024, published vide number G.S.R. 
349(E) in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, Section 3, Sub-section (i), dated the 27th June, 2024; 


And whereas, the designated authority, vide initiation notification F. No. 07/20/2026-DGTR, dated the 28th 
September, 2026, published in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part I, Section |, has initiated an anti-circumvention 
investigation under section 9A(lA) of the Customs Tariff Act, 975 (5] of 975) read with rules 25 and 26 of the 
Customs Tariff (Identification, Assessment and Collection of Anti-Dumping Duty on Dumped Articles and for 
Determination of Injury) Rules, 995 (hereinafter referred to as the said rules), concerning alleged circumvention of the 
anti-dumping duty imposed on import of the subject goods by imports of the product under investigation exported from 
Malaysia; 


And whereas, the designated authority has observed prima facie evidence of country-based circumvention through 
Malaysia and has recommended provisional assessment of imports of the product under investigation exported from 
Malaysia and obtaining an appropriate guarantee from the importers in accordance with sub-rule (4A) of rule 26 of the 
said rules; 


Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (A) of section 9A of the Customs Tariff Act, 
975, read with sub-rule (4A) of rule 26 of the said rules, the Central Government, after considering the aforesaid 
recommendation of the designated authority, hereby orders that, pending the outcome of the said anti-circumvention 
investigation, imports into India of the product under investigation, namely Alloy Steel Chisel/tool and Hydraulic Rock 
Breaker in fully assembled condition, including the seven assemblies/sub-assemblies/components of hydraulic rock 
breakers as listed in the Explanation below, exported from Malaysia, shall be subjected to provisional assessment till a 
decision under sub-rule (3) of rule 27 of the said rules is taken by the Central Government. 


2. The provisional assessment shall be subject to furnishing such guarantee as the proper officer of customs deems 
fit, for payment of the anti-dumping duty, if any, that may become payable consequent upon the recommendations of 
the designated authority and the decision of the Central Government under sub-rule (3) of rule 27 of the said rules. 


“Explanation. - For the purposes of this notification, the seven assemblies/sub-assemblies/components of hydraulic rock 
breakers referred to above are the following, namely: - 


(a) Front head, 

(b) Back head, 

(c) Piston for hydraulic cylinder or rock breaker, 

(d) Cylinder body or hydraulic unit (Hydraulic body consists of front head, back head, cylinder and piston), 
(e) Bracket,

S.O. 6069(E).— In exercise of powers conferred by sub-section () of section 3A of the National Highways

stretch of land from Km. |80.00 to Km. 90.00 (land Acquisition Padhar) in the District of MANDI in the state of 
HIMACHAL PRADESH, hereby declares its intention to acquire such land. 


Any person interested in the said land may, within twenty-one days from the date of publication of this 
notification in the Official Gazette, object to the use of such land for the aforesaid purpose under sub-section(l) of 
section 3C of the said Act. 


Every such objection shall be made to the Competent Authority, namely, CALA-cum-SDM Padhar in writing 
and shall set out the grounds thereof and the Competent Authority shall give the objector an opportunity of being 
heard, either in person or by a legal practitioner, and may, after hearing all such objections and after making such 
further enquiry, if any, as the Competent Authority thinks necessary, by order, either allow or disallow the objections. 


Any order made by the Competent Authority under sub-section (2) of section 3C of the said Act shall 
be final. 


The land plans and other details of the land to be acquired under their notification are available and can be 
inspected by the interested person at the aforesaid office of the Competent Authority.

NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 5th November, 2026 


S.O. 6052(E).— In exercise of the powers conferred by sub section (1) of section 3A of the National Highways 
Act, 1956 (48 of 1956)(hereafter referred to as the said act), the Central Government, after being satisfied that for the 
public purpose, the land, the brief description of which is given in the Schedule below, is required for building 
(widening/2-Laning with paved shoulder), maintenance, management and operation of the National Highway No.144A 
in the stretch of land from Km 90.150 to Km 116.980 Akhnoor - Poonch Road (Package-V) of National Highway No. 
144A in the district of Rajouri in the Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir, hereby declares its intention to acquire such 
land; 


Any person interested in the said land may, within twenty-one days from the date of publication of this 
notification in the Official Gazette, object to the use of such land for the aforesaid purpose under sub-section (1) of 
section 3 C of the said act; 


Every such objection shall be made to the Competent Authority, namely, the Deputy Commissioner, Rajouri, 
in writing and shall set out the grounds there of and the Competent Authority shall give the objector an opportunity of 
being heard, either in person or by a legal practitioner, and may after hearing all such objections and after making such 
further enquiry, if any, as the competent authority thinks necessary, by order, either allow or disallow the objections. 


Any order made by the competent authority under sub-section (2) of section 3 C of the said act shall be final. 


The land plans and other details of the land covered under this notification are available and can be inspected 
by the interested person at the aforesaid office of the competent authority.

NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 5th November, 2026 


S.O. 6056(E).— In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (1) of section 3A of the National 
Highways Act,1956 (48 of 1956) (hereafter referred to as the said Act), the Central Government, after being 
satisfied that for the public purpose, the land, the brief description of which is given in the Schedule below, 
is required for building(widening/2-4 laning with paved shoulder), maintenance, management and operation 
of National Highway no.543 in the stretch of land from Km. 0+000 to km. 91+700 (Dindori to Mandla 
Road) (Tehsil-Ghughari) in the district of Mandla in the state of MADHYA PRADESH, hereby declares 
its intention to acquire such land. 


Any person interested in the said land may, within twenty-one days from the date of publication of 
this notification in the Official Gazette, object to the use of such land for the aforesaid purpose under sub- 
section(1) of section 3C of the said Act. 


Every such objection shall be made to the Competent Authority, namely, the Sub Divisional 
Magistrate Ghughari, District Mandla, in writing and shall set out the grounds thereof and the Competent 
Authority shall give the objector an opportunity of being heard, either in person or by a legal practitioner, 
and may, after hearing all such objections and after making such further enquiry, if any, as the Competent 
Authority thinks necessary, by order, eitherallow or disallow the objections. 


Any order made by the Competent Authority under sub-section (2) of section 3C of the said Act 
shall be final. 


The land plans and other details of the land covered under this nitification are available and can be 
inspected by by the interested person at the aforesaid office of the Competent Authority.

conferred by sub-section (l) of section 20E of the said Act, the Central Government hereby declare that the land 
specified in the schedule annexed hereto shall be acquired for the aforesaid purpose;

MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS 
[North Western Railway (Construction Organization)] 
NOTIFICATION 

Jaipur, the 6th November, 2026 
S.O. 6084(E).— Whereas, by the notification of the Government of India, in the Ministry of Railways 
(North Western Railway, Construction organization), Notification number, 5.0. 479 (E) dated 257 August 2026 
published in Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, section 3 Sub-section (ii), dated the 257 August 2026 (hereinafter 
referred to as the said notification) and issued under sub-section (l) of section 20A of the Railway (Amendment) Act 
2008 (I of 2008) and Railway Act 989 (24 of 989) (hereinafter referred to as the said Act), the Central Government 
declares its intention to acquire the land specified in the schedule annexed to the said notification for the purpose of 
execution, maintenance, management and operation of Special Railway Project, namely "Luni-Samdari-Bhildi 


Doubling Project of the District Jodhpur in the state of Rajasthan. 


And whereas, the substance of the said notification was published in daily newspapers namely “Rajasthan 


Patrika ” and “Dainik Bhaskar” dated 02.09.2026 sub section (4) of section 20A of the said Act. 


And whereas, out of the surveys of the villages mentioned in the schedule annexed with this notification, all 
the objections were received within the stipulated time period by Competent Authority and accordingly, the same was 


disposed by Competent Authority. 


8 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 30) | 


And, whereas, in pursuance of sub-section (l) of section 20E of the said Act, the competent authority has 


submitted its report to the Central Government; 


Now, therefore, upon receipt of the said report of the competent authority, and in exercise of the powers 
conferred by sub-section (l) of section 20E of the said Act, the Central Government hereby declare that the land 
specified in the schedule annexed hereto shall be acquired for the aforesaid purpose; 

And, further, in pursuance of sub-section (2) of section 20E of the said Act, the Central Government hereby 


declares that on publication of this notification in the official Gazette, the land specified in the schedule annexed hereto 
shall vest absolutely in the Central Government free from all encumbrances.

का.आ. 6085(अ).--- रेलवे अधिनियम, 1989 (1989 का 24) (इसके बाद उक्त अधिनियम के रूप में संदर्भित) की 

धारा 20ए की उप-धारा ()) द्वारा प्रदत्त शक्तियों का प्रयोग करते हुए, केंद्र सरकार इस बात से संतुष्ट होने के पश्चात्‌ कि 
सार्वजनिक उद्देश्य के लिए भूमि, जिसका संक्षिप्त विवरण इसके साथ संलग्न अनुसूची में दिया गया है, तेलंगाना राज्य के 
वनपर्ती जिले में विशेष रेलवे परियोजना अर्थात्‌ मुदखेड-डोन रेलपथ दोहरीकरण के निष्पादन के लिए आवश्यक है, एतद्दारा 
ऐसी भूमि का अधिग्रहण करने की अपनी इच्छा की घोषणा करती है; 

उक्त भूमि में हितप्रद्ध कोई भी व्यक्ति उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 20डी की उप-धार (1) के अंतर्गत उपर्युक्त उद्देश्य के 
लिए ऐसी भूमि के अधिग्रहण और उपयोग के संबंध में सरकारी राजपत्र में इस अधिसूचना के प्रकाशन की तारीख से तीस 
दिनों की अवधी के भीतर भू-अर्जन में अपनी आपत्ति दर्ज करा सकता है. 

ऐसी प्रत्येक आपत्ति, सक्षम प्राधिकारी, अर्थात्‌ राजस्व मंडल अधिकारी, वनपर्ती जिला, तेलंगाना राज्य को लिखित 
रूप में दी जाएगी और उसके आधारों को निर्धारित की जाएगी और सक्षम प्राधिकारी, अर्थात्‌ राजस्व मंडल अधिकारी, 
वनपर्ती जिला आपत्तिकर्ता को व्यक्तिगत रूप से या कानूनी व्यवसायी द्वारा सुनवाई का अवसर देगा और ऐसी सभी आपत्तियों 
को सुनने के बाद तथा आगे ऐसी जांच करने के बाद, यदि सक्षम प्राधिकारी यह आवश्यक समझता है तो वह किसी आदेश 
द्वारा आपत्तियों को स्वीकार या अस्वीकार कर सकता है.

MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS

NOTIFICATION 
Secunderabad, the 6th November, 2026 


S.O. 6085(E).— In exercise of the power conferred by Sub-Section (I) of section 20A of the Railways 
Act,1989(24 of 1989) (hereafter referred as in as the said Act.), Central Government, after being satisfied that for the 
public purpose, the land, the brief description of which is given in the schedule annexed hereto, is required for execution 
of the special railway project, Medkhed — Dhone Doubling of track in Wanaparthy district in the state of Telangana, 
hereby declares its intention to acquire such lands. 


Any person interested in the said land may, within a period of Thirty days from the date of publication of this 
notification in the official Gazette, raise objection to the acquisition and use of such land for the aforesaid purposes 
under sub-section (1) of section 20D of the said Act. 


Every such objection shall be made to the Competent Authority, namely, the Revenu Divisional Officer, 
Wanaparthy district, Telangana State, in writing and shall set out the grounds thereof and the Competent Authority 
Revenue Divisional Officer, Wanaparthy District shall give the objector an opportunity of being heard, either in person 
or by a legal practitioner, and may, after hearing all such objections and after making such further enquiry, if any, as the 
competent authority thinks necessary by order, either allow or disallow the objections. 


Any order made by the Competent Authority under sub-section (II) of section 20 D of the said Act shall be final. 


The land plans and other details of land covered under this notification are available and can be inspected by 
the interested person at the aforesaid office of Competent Authority.

to

Introduction 


1.1.Interconnection in telecommunications refers to commercial and technical arrangements that allow authorised

entities or licensees to connect their telecommunication equipment, networks, and services, enabling their users 
to access the users, services, and networks of other authorized entities or licensees. 


The Register of Interconnect Agreements Regulations, 1999, were notified on 317 August 1999, and came into 
force on 17 September 1999, to establish a regulatory framework for registration of interconnect agreements 
entered into between service providers. These regulations prescribe the modalities for the maintenance of the 
register of interconnect agreements between service providers and matters connected therewith. These 
regulations cover important aspects relating to the submission and registration of interconnect agreements, 
maintenance of the register by the Authority, contents of the interconnect agreement to be kept confidential, 
inspection of interconnect agreements, and related processes. These regulations were subsequently amended 
on 3 February 2004, 31% December 2004, and 47 March 2005. 


This Explanatory Memorandum sets out the background, rationale, and considerations underlying the Register 
of Interconnect Agreements (Fourth Amendment) Regulations, 2026, to enable stakeholders to understand the 
Authority’s approach in formulating these regulations. 


Present exercise to review the regulatory framework for the register of interconnect agreements in India 


The Authority issued a pre-consultation paper dated 377 April 2025 and subsequently issued a consultation 
paper on the ‘Review of existing TRAI Regulations on Interconnection matters’ on 10 November 2025 to 
seek the views of stakeholders on different aspects of these Regulations. The stakeholders were requested to 
submit their written comments and counter-comments by the extended last dates of 157 December 2025 and 
297 December 2025, respectively. An open house discussion was held with the stakeholders on 287 January 
2026. The issues raised in the consultation paper, submissions of stakeholders through comments and counter- 
comments and during the open house discussion, have been examined in the succeeding paragraphs. 


Analysis of the issues related to the regulatory framework for the register of interconnect agreements 


In the consultation paper dated 10 November 2025, the Authority sought views from the stakeholders on the 
various issues related to the regulatory framework for the register of interconnect agreements. The relevant 
issues which have been discussed in this explanatory memorandum are as follows: 
a. Examination of the need for online submission, inspection, and obtaining a copy of the relevant 
portions of the interconnect agreements and modifications thereto. 
b. Examination of the fee for seeking inspection and charges for obtaining copies of the relevant portions 
from the register. 
c. Necessary financial disincentive framework.

a) Views of stakeholders on the need for online submission, inspection, obtaining copies of relevant portions 
of interconnect agreements and modifications thereto, review of fees for inspection, charges for obtaining 
copies, and necessary financial disincentive framework. 


3.4.6. Many stakeholders submitted that the existing system of floppy disk and paper-based processes of 
submission of interconnect agreements and modifications thereto should be dispensed with, and 
needs to be transitioned to a fully digital, online framework. Stakeholders have emphasized that the 
current system is outdated and inefficient, and that it requires replacement with digital processes 
aligned with evolving technological and regulatory practices. Further, stakeholders have broadly 
supported the adoption of a centralized online portal to facilitate end-to-end digital processes, 
including submission, acknowledgment, tracking, inspection, and access to interconnect agreements. 


3.4.7. A few stakeholders have further highlighted the importance of adopting submission of an electronic 
copy of documents in place of wet-signed physical documents as submission of physical documents 
leads to delays and inefficiencies. 


3.4.8. Some stakeholders have also emphasized the need for submission of searchable documents in place 
of non-searchable scanned copies, as searchable scanned documents facilitate efficiency in reviewing 
and retrieving information therein. 


3.4.9. Regarding the timeline for submission, a few stakeholders proposed that electronic copies of 
interconnect agreements should be submitted through the TRAI portal within 15 or 7 days of 
execution. 


3.4.10. Regarding the fees for seeking inspection and for obtaining copies of the relevant portions of the 
Register, many stakeholders submitted that any associated fees should be nominal, reasonable, and 
clearly specified. 

3.4.11. A few stakeholders recommended facilitating public access to non-confidential records through 
electronic means only and dispensing with inspection and copying fees in the digital environment. 


3.4.12. Regarding the incorporation of provisions for necessary financial disincentives into interconnection 
regulations to deter non-compliance, some stakeholders stated that financial disincentives are not 
required, arguing that a mature telecom market and existing regulatory provisions are sufficient to 
ensure compliance without additional penalties. Other stakeholders argued in favour of incorporation 
of a necessary financial disincentive framework. One stakeholder stated that appropriate provisions 
for financial disincentives should be incorporated into the regulation to deter non-compliance by 
private and PSU operators alike. Other stakeholders recommended financial disincentives as a 
deterrent to ensure compliance with inter-operator rights and obligations. They emphasized that 
financial disincentives should be applied only in extreme cases, after giving service providers an 
opportunity for a hearing and conclusive proof of non-compliance.

The existing provisions requiring submission of paper-based agreements together with soft copies 
on 3.5” floppy/diskette are obsolete, technologically outdated, and no longer aligned with prevailing 
practices. The continued reliance on physical documentation and outdated storage media results in 
procedural inefficiencies. These inefficiencies can be avoided by online submissions and dispensing 
with the process of physical submissions of interconnect agreements. Accordingly, it is decided that 
submission of interconnect agreements and modifications thereto, under these regulations, shall 
henceforth be made only in electronic form through a portal. This framework is expected to facilitate 
streamlined submission, handling, maintenance, and retrieval of records, while reducing dependence 
on physical documentation and outdated technological formats. 


In order to ensure continued accessibility and convenience for the public, inspection of the register 
and obtaining extracts from the relevant portions thereof should be permitted in both physical and 
electronic modes through a portal. Enabling access through electronic mode, in addition to the 
existing physical mode, would provide greater flexibility, facilitate efficient retrieval and 
dissemination of information, and promote ease of access for users. Further, provisions governing 
the inspection of the register and obtaining extracts therefrom shall remain similar for both physical 
mode and electronic mode through a portal. 


It is observed that text-searchable electronic documents in standard formats, such as portable 
document format (PDF), would enhance ease of processing and efficiency in record management. 
Accordingly, it is decided that all service providers shall submit a text-searchable PDF copy of their 
interconnect agreements and modifications thereto on the TRAI portal within the period specified 
in these regulations. 


The proposal to shorten the timeline for submitting interconnect agreements has been examined. In 
this regard, some of the stakeholders have suggested a timeline of fifteen days from the date of 
execution of the interconnect agreement, whereas some other stakeholders have suggested a timeline 
of seven days. It is noted that the existing timeline of thirty days was prescribed at a time when the 
interconnect agreements were required to be submitted in physical form, along with a soft copy ina 
floppy or diskette. It has now been decided that the interconnect agreements shall be submitted in an 
online manner through a portal. Accordingly, the time needed for submission would be substantially 
reduced. Considering this, a timeline of fifteen days from the date of execution or modification of 
the interconnect agreement would be appropriate in an online environment. At the same time, the 
service providers will be free to submit the interconnect agreements earlier than the prescribed 
timeline, if they are in a position to do so. 


It is noted that while the Authority may specify formats for seeking disaggregated information 
relating to interconnect agreements under regulation 7, the existing provisions do not explicitly 
provide for the furnishing of such information within a specified timeframe. Accordingly, a provision 
has been inserted requiring service providers to furnish such information in the specified format and 
within the period specified by the Authority, so as to facilitate effective maintenance and timely 
updation of the Register. 


With reference to the fee for inspection of the register and charges for obtaining copies of extracts 
from the register, it is noted that the prescribed fees for inspection and charges for obtaining copies 
of the relevant portions of the Register have remained unchanged since these regulations were 
notified in 1999.

It has been decided to rationalize and align the applicable fee for obtaining copies of the relevant 
portions of the Register with the fee prescribed under the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India 
(Access to Information) Regulation, 2005, in order to ensure uniformity of the applicable charges 
between the said Regulation and the Register of Interconnect Agreements Regulations, 1999. 
Accordingly, it is decided to revise the fee for obtaining copies of extracts from the Register and 
inspection of documents under the Register of Interconnect Agreements Regulations, 1999. 


It is recognized that the inspection of records and provision of extracts, whether in physical or 
electronic form, involves administrative and operational costs in maintaining and facilitating such 
arrangements. Accordingly, a reasonable and standardized fee framework remains necessary. It is 
therefore decided that the fee structure for inspection of, and obtaining copies of extracts from, the 
relevant portions of the Register shall be rupees one thousand five hundred per hour or part thereof, 
and rupees five hundred per page, respectively. Where the duration of inspection exceeds one hour, 
the fee shall be charged at the same rate for every additional hour or part thereof. This fee structure 
is broadly aligned with the fee structure prescribed under the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India 
(Access to Information) Regulation, 2005. 


It is noted that the term "consumer", as presently defined in these regulations, is not aligned with the 
terminology used in the current telecommunications framework. Accordingly, the definition of 
"consumer" has been replaced with the definition of "user" and consequential changes have been 
made to align the terminology used in these regulations with the current telecommunications 
framework and to ensure consistency across the regulatory framework. 


It has also been decided to include particulars of the telecommunication service authorisations 
specified in the interconnect agreements in Part I of the Register, to facilitate identification of the 
authorisations to which the registered agreements relate. 


The Authority has examined the comments received from stakeholders regarding the necessary 
financial disincentive framework in the Register of Interconnect Agreements Regulations, 1999, as 
amended from time to time. The financial disincentives play an important role in ensuring regulatory 
compliance by service providers, as well as in safeguarding the rights of service providers under the 
interconnection framework. 


It is decided that financial disincentives be imposed on a case-by-case basis, after providing the 
concerned service provider a reasonable opportunity to present its explanation. It is also decided that 
the financial disincentive framework be introduced to ensure proportionality and deterrence. The 
quantum of financial disincentive should be reasonable and balanced so as to serve as an effective 
deterrent against non-compliance, without being either negligible or unduly burdensome. 


The Authority has considered the nature and potential impact of non-compliance with the provisions 
of these regulations. The provisions covered under regulation 5 and regulation 6 relate to various 
aspects of submission of interconnect agreements and modifications to them for registration and 
inclusion in the Register. These requirements are important for keeping the Register complete, 
accurate and up to date. Any non-compliance with these regulations, i.e., failure to submit the 
interconnect agreement and modifications, within the period specified by the Authority, may directly 
and significantly affect the proper functioning of the interconnection framework. The Authority is, 
therefore, of the view that a higher financial disincentive is appropriate for non-compliance of 
regulation 5 or regulation 6. 


On the other hand, regulation 7 relates to furnishing of disaggregated information in the prescribed 
formats pertaining to interconnect agreements. This information is important for maintaining the

requirements, i.e., failure to furnish the information within the period specified by the Authority, 
generally has a comparatively limited direct impact on the interconnection framework. The Authority 
is, therefore, of the view that a lower financial disincentive is appropriate for non-compliance with 
regulation 7. 


It has also been considered that a fixed financial disincentive, irrespective of the duration of the 
contravention, may not adequately distinguish between a short delay and continued non-compliance. 
Therefore, a graded financial disincentive has been prescribed, with a lower rate for delay up to fifteen 
days and a higher rate where the delay continues beyond fifteen days. The higher rate for prolonged 
delay is intended to encourage service providers to take timely corrective action and ensure 
compliance at the earliest. 


For clarity, the maximum financial disincentive may be determined on an accumulated basis according 
to the number of days of delay. For example, in the case of a contravention where the applicable 
maximum per day rates are 50,000 per day for the first fifteen days and %1,00,000 per day for each 
day beyond fifteen days, if the delay is for twenty days, the financial disincentive would be 7.5 lakh 
for the first fifteen days and %5 lakh for the next five days, making a total maximum financial 
disincentive of =12.5 lakh, subject to the applicable ceiling. 


At the same time, there should be a reasonable ceiling on the financial disincentive so that the financial 
liability does not continue to increase indefinitely. Accordingly, an overall ceiling of rupees twenty- 
five lakh per Service Area for each instance of failure to furnish, within the period specified by the 
Authority, the information sought under regulation 7 and rupees one crore per Service Area for each 
instance of contravention of regulation 5 or regulation 6 has been prescribed. To give effect to the 
above, the following Schedule has been incorporated for financial disincentive:

The financial disincentive imposed on a service provider should be paid within twenty-one days from 
the date of issue of the order or within the period specified in the order. To ensure timely payment and 
discourage delay, simple interest on the outstanding amount of financial disincentive has been 
provided in case of delayed payment. It is considered that linking the rate of interest to the one-year 
Marginal Cost of Funds-based Lending Rate (MCLR) of State Bank of India, with an additional two 
percent, would provide an objective basis for determining the applicable rate. Accordingly, the service 
provider shall be liable to pay simple interest on the outstanding amount at the said rate applicable at 
the beginning of the financial year in which the last day of the stipulated period falls. It has also been 
provided that a part of the month shall be reckoned as a full calendar month for calculation of interest 
and a month shall be reckoned as an English calendar month.

that issues relating to the interpretation or application of the provisions of these regulations may arise. 
Accordingly, provisions enabling review of these regulations and issuance of necessary clarifications 
or guidelines for removal of difficulties have been included.

Bhopal, the 3rd November, 2026 


F. ॥४०.।३ INDB-BNI/LA/Gazette/2l/Work Correspondence date 03//2026.— Whereas by the 
notification of the Rail Vikas Nigam Limited, notification No. F. No.l3 INDB-BNI/LA/Gazette/l5/Work 
Correspondence New Delhi Dated 07 April, 2026 published in Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part III, Section 4, 
(hereinafter referred to as the said notification) under Sub Section (l) of Section 20A of the Railways Act 989 (Railway 
Amendment Act 2008) (hereinafter referred to as the said Act), the Central Government declared its intention to acquire 
the land specified in the Schedule annexed to the said notification for execution, maintenance, management and operation 
of "Indore-Budni New 3.0. Railway Line" in the district Indore, Dewas & Sehore in the State of Madhya Pradesh 


And, whereas, the substance of the said notification was published in daily local Newspapers ‘‘Raj Express” 
and ‘‘Navduniya” dated 2] April 2026 & 2! April 2026 under Sub Section (4) of Section 20A of the said act; 


And, whereas, no objection has been received by the competent authority; 


And, whereas, in pursuance of sub-section (l) of section 20E of the said Act, the competent authority has 
submitted its report to the Central Government: 


Now, therefore, upon receipt of the said report of the competent authority, and in exercise of the powers 
conferred by sub-section (l) of section 20E of the said Act, the Central Government hereby declares that the land 
specified in the schedule annexed hereto shall be acquired for the aforesaid purpose; 


And, further, in pursuance of Sub Section (2) of section 20E of the said Act, the Central Government hereby 
declares that on publication of this notification in the official Gazette, the land specified in the schedule annexed here 
to shall vest absolutely in the Central Government free from all encumbrances.

की उप-धारा (4) के अंतर्गत दैनिक समाचार पत्रों, नवभारत (हिन्दी) बिलासपुर संस्करण में दिनांक 20.03.2026 को, 
टाइम्स ऑफ इंडिया (अंग्रेजी) रायपुर संस्करण में दिनांक 20.03.2026 को और नवीन कदम (हिन्दी) रायगढ़ संस्करण में 
दिनांक 20.03.2026 को प्रकाशित किया गया था 


और जबकि, निर्धारित समयावधि के भीतर आपत्तियां प्राप्त हुईं और उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 209 के 
अंतर्गत सक्षम प्राधिकारी द्वारा उनका निपटारा कर दिया गया है। 


और जबकि, उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 207 की उप-धारा (1) के अनुसरण में, सक्षम प्राधिकारी ने अपनी 
रिपोर्ट केंद्र सरकार को प्रस्तुत कर दी है 


अब इसलिए, सक्षम प्राधिकारी की उक्त रिपोर्ट प्राप्त होने पर, और रेलवे अधिनियम, 1989 की धारा 
20E की उप-धारा (1) द्वारा प्रदत्त शक्तियों का प्रयोग करते हुए, केंद्र सरकार WAIT घोषणा करती है कि इसके 
साथ संलग्न अनुसूची में विनिर्दिष्ट भूमि का अर्जन उपर्युक्त प्रयोजन के लिए किया जाएगा 


और आगे, उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 2OE की उप-धारा (2) के अनुसरण में, केंद्र सरकार VARI घोषणा 
करती है कि इस अधिसूचना के शासकीय राजपपत्र में प्रकाशित होने पर, संलग्न अनुसूची में विनिर्दिष्ट भूमि सभी 
भारों से मुक्त होकर पूर्ण रूप से केंद्र सरकार में निहित हो जाएगी।

MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS 
(South East Central Railway) 
NOTIFICATION 
Bilaspur, the 5th November, 2026 
Notification under Section 20E of the Railways Act, 1989 


S.O. 6097(E).— Whereas, by the notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of Railways 
(South East Central Railway) number S.O. 1195 (E), dated 7th March 2026, published in the Gazette of 
India (Extraordinary), Part-II, Section 3, Sub-section (ii) (hereinafter referred to as the said notification), 
issued under sub-section (1) of Section 20A of the Railways Act, 1989 (24 of 1989) (hereinafter referred to 
as the said Act), the Central Government declared its intention to acquire the land specified in the Schedule 
annexed to the said notification in the villages of Kunjemura, Pata, Libra and Jhinkabahal in the State of 
Chhattisgarh, for the purpose of execution of the special railway project, namely "Sardega - Bhalumuda 
New Double Line (37.24 km), South East Central Railway". 


And whereas, the substance of the said notification number 1143, dated 7th March 2026, was 
published under sub-section (4) of Section 20A of the said Act in the daily newspapers Navbharat (Hindi), 
Bilaspur edition, on 20.03.2026, The Times of India (English), Raipur edition, on 20.03.2026, and Naveen 
Kadam (Hindi), Raigarh edition, on 20.03.2026 


And whereas, objections were received within the prescribed period and have been disposed of by 
the competent authority under Section 20D of the said Act. 


And whereas, in pursuance of sub-section (1) of Section 20E of the said Act, the competent 
authority has submitted its report to the Central Government 


Now, therefore, on receipt of the said report of the competent authority, and in exercise of the 
powers conferred by sub-section (1) of Section 20E of the Railways Act, 1989, the Central Government 
hereby declares that the land specified in the Schedule annexed hereto shall be acquired for the aforesaid 
purpose 


And further, in pursuance of sub-section (2) of Section 20E of the said Act, the Central Government 
hereby declares that, on publication of this notification in the Official Gazette, the land specified in the 
annexed Schedule shall vest absolutely in the Central Government, free from all encumbrances.

DEENDAYAL PORT AUTHORITY 
NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 30th October, 2026 


F. No. GA/PS/9125(RSP)/2024—Whereas, the draft of the Deendayal Port Authority Employees 
(Recruitment, Seniority and Promotion) Regulations, 2024, was published, under sub-section (1) of section 72 of the 
Major Port Authorities Act, 2021 (1 of 2021), vide Notification dated the 4" November 2024 (extra No.116) and 
corrigendum dated the 25" November 2024 (extra No.157), in the Gujarat Government Gazette, Extraordinary, Part 
IV-C, inviting objections or suggestions from all person likely to be affected thereby, before the expiry of a period of 
thirty days from the date on which the copies of the Gujarat Government Gazette, in which the said draft regulations 
were published, were made available to the public; 


And whereas, the copies of the said Gujarat Government Gazette were made available to the public on the 
47 November 2024: 


And whereas, no objection or suggestion have been received from the public within the said period of thirty 
days; 


Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (1) and clauses (c) and (i) of sub-section 
(2) of section 72 read with section 18 of Major Port Authorities Act, 2021 (1 of 2021), and in supersession of the 
Deendayal Port Trust Employees (Recruitment, Seniority and Promotion) Regulations 2009 except as respects things 
done or omitted to be done before such supersession, the Board of Deendayal Port Authority hereby makes the 
following regulations, namely: - 


1. Short title and commencement - (1) These regulations may be called the Deendayal Port Authority 
Employees’ (Recruitment, Seniority and Promotion) Regulations, 2026. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Gazette of India. 


2. Application - These regulations shall apply to all posts whether temporary or permanent created by the Board 
including those covered by sub-section (1) of section 18 of the Act. 


3. Definition — (1) In these regulations, unless the context otherwise requires, - 
(a) "Act" means the Major Port Authorities Act, 2021 (1 of 2021); 
(b) “Analogous Post” means a post of which the duties and level of responsibilities and the pay ranges 


are comparable to those of the post to which selection is to be made; 


(c) "Appointing Authority" in relation to any grade or post means the authority empowered under the 
Kandla Port Trust Employees (Classification, Control and Appeal) Regulations, 2004, to make 
appointment to that grade or post; 


(d) "Board", "Chairperson", "Deputy Chairperson" and "Head of Department" have the meanings 
respectively assigned to them under the Act; 


(e) "Class I Posts", "Class II Posts" “Class-IIl posts" and "Class- IV posts" shall have the same meanings 
as assigned to them under Regulation 4 of the Kandla Port Trust Employees (Classification, Control 


and Appeal) Regulations, 2004; 


(f) "Departmental Promotion Committee" means a Committee constituted under regulation 26 for the 
purposes of making recommendations for promotion to or confirmation in any grade or post; 


(g) "direct recruit" means a person recruited on the basis of a competitive examination or test and/or 
interview by Services Selection Committee; 


(h) "employee" means an employee of the Board;

"lien" means the title of an employee to hold on regular basis, either immediately or on the

Provided that the title to hold a regular post shall be subject to the condition that the junior

entitled is more than the posts available in that grade; 


"permanent employee" means an employee who has been substantively appointed to a permanent 
post; 


“regular service”, in relation to any grade, means the period or periods of service in that grade 
rendered after selection and appointment thereto under these regulations according to the prescribed 


procedure for regular appointment to that grade and includes any period or periods - 


(i) taken into account for the purpose of seniority in case of those already in service at the

(ii) during which an employee would have held a post in that grade but for being on leave or 
otherwise not being available for holding such post; 


"Schedule" means the Schedule appended to these regulations; 


"Scheduled Castes" and "Scheduled Tribes" shall have the meanings respectively assigned to them 
in clauses (24) and (25) of article 366 of the Constitution of India; 


"Select list" in relation to any grade or post means the select list prepared in accordance with 
regulation 13 for that grade or post; 


"Selection Post" means a post declared as such under regulation 5; 
"Services Selection Committee" means the Committee constituted under regulation 12 for the 
selection of candidates by means of a written test, a trade test and interview or both for appointment 


to posts reserved for direct recruitment; 


"temporary employee" means an employee holding a temporary post or officiating in a permanent 
post or on probation in his appointment in the service of the Board. 


The words and expressions used herein and not defined in the regulations but defined in the Act, shall 
have the same meanings respectively assigned to them in the said Act. 


Manner of appointment - (1) All appointments to the posts to which these regulations apply shall be made 
in accordance with the provisions of these regulations, either by promotion or by absorption or deputation or 
direct recruitment. 


(2) The vacancies in respect of posts of Head of Department and posts one level below to the Head of 
Department, shall be filled by “Composite method of recruitment” through promotion or transfer on absorption 
basis failing which by deputation from the employees of the Major Ports, the Central Government, State 
Governments, Autonomous Bodies, Government Companies and failing both by direct recruitment. 


(3) The promotion or transfer on absorption shall be made from the officers from the Major Port Authority 
fulfilling the eligibility criteria prescribed in the Schedule annexed to these regulations. 


(4) The deputation shall be of employees from the Major Ports, the Central Government, State Governments 
or Autonomous Bodies or Government Companies fulfilling the eligibility criteria prescribed for the post:

Provided that an employee of a Board of any Major Port Authority shall not be eligible for deputation 
to the Head of Department level post in the Major Port Authority. 


(5) The normal period of deputation shall be three years, which shall be extendable to four years and in 
exceptional circumstances, this may be extended to five years by the Central Government in the case of a post, 
the incumbent of which is regarded as the Head of Department and by the Chairperson in the case of any other 
post below the level of Head of Department. 


5. Schedule - (1) The manner of appointment i.e. whether by direct recruitment or promotion or absorption or 
deputation, the educational qualifications, age, training, experience, classification of posts whether selection 
posts or non - selection posts and other matters connected with the said appointment shall be same as specified 
in the Schedule annexed to these regulations. 


(2) In respect of Class-II, Class-III and Class-IV posts, the manner of appointment shall be as laid down by 
the Board from time to time. 


(3) The authorized permanent and temporary strength of the various grades shall be as specified in the list of 
Employees prepared under the provisions of section 20 of the Major Port Authorities Act, 2021, and the 
eligibility requirements prescribed for direct recruitment shall apply in the case of promotion to the extent 
mentioned in column 9 of the Schedule and requirement of experience for promotion shall be as prescribed in 
column 12 of the said Schedule: 


Provided that the prescribed upper age limits may be relaxed by the Central Government in case of 
Head of Departments and by Chairperson in all other cases for reasons to be recorded in writing for direct 
recruitment or absorption or deputation as under,- 


(i) upto five years where the minimum experience prescribed is ten years or more and upto three 
years where the minimum experience prescribed is five to nine years; 


(ii) 11116 case of a candidate who is an ex-serviceman, and who has put in not less than six months’ 
continuous service in the Defence Forces upto the extent of the service rendered by him in the 
Defence Forces plus three years where the vacancy to be filled is a vacancy reserved for such 
ex-servicemen and dependents of those killed in action and upto the extent of the service 
rendered by him in the Defence Forces, where the vacancy to be filled is an unreserved 
vacancy; and 


(iii) ॥ the case of a candidate belonging to the Scheduled Castes or the Scheduled Tribes or Other 
Backward Classes, in accordance with such orders as the Central Government may issue from 
time to time in this regard: 


Provided further that the requirement of experience is relaxable at the discretion of the Central 
Government in the case of candidates belonging to the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes if at any 
stage of selection, the Central Government is of the opinion that sufficient number of candidates from these 
communities possessing the requisite experience are not likely to be available to fill up the posts reserved for 
them. 


6. Roster of vacancies - A roster shall be maintained for each grade to show whether a particular vacancy shall 
be filled by direct recruitment or promotion; provided that, if a vacancy which is reserved for direct recruitment cannot 
be filled by direct recruitment, it may be filled by promotion and the next vacancy shall be filled by direct recruitment 
and similarly in the case of a vacancy reserved for promotion but cannot be filled by promotion method, the same may 
be filled by direct recruitment. 


7. Reservation - (1) The orders issued by the Central Government from time to time for reservation of 

posts under it, whether to be filled by direct recruitment or promotion in respect of the candidates belonging 
to Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes shall apply mutatis mutandis to all appointments covered under these 
regulations. 


(2) The orders issued by the Central Government from time to time for the reservation of posts under these 
regulations in favor of Other Backward Classes, ex-Servicemen and dependents of those killed in action, Sportsmen

and physically handicapped persons shall also apply mutatis mutandis to appointments covered under these regulations 
and to which direct recruitment is made. 


8. Nationality, character, physical fitness etc. for direct recruitment - 
(1) In order to be eligible for direct recruitment to any grade or post, a candidate shall besides educational 
qualification and other criteria be- 
(a) a citizen of India; or 
(b) a subject of Nepal; or 
(c) a subject of Bhutan; or 
(d) a Tibetan refugee who came over to India before the 1“January 1962 with the intention of 
permanently settling in India; or 
(e) A person of Indian origin who has migrated from Pakistan, Burma, Sri Lanka or the East 


African countries of Kenya, Uganda, the United Republic of Tanzania, Zambia, Malawi, Zaire and 
Ethiopia and Vietnam with the intention of permanently settling in India: 


Provided that a candidate belonging to categories (b), (c), (d) and (e) shall be a person in whose 
favour a certificate of eligibility has been issued by the Government of India; 


Provided further that in case a candidate in whose case the submission of proof of nationality or 
a certificate of eligibility is necessary may be provisionally appointed, pending submission of such 
certificate for a period not exceeding one year. 


(2) The Chairperson may, with the prior approval of the Central Government, modify or waive any of 
the requirements of sub regulation (1) when an appointment for work of a special nature is to be made and it 
is not practicable to obtain a suitable candidate who fulfills the requirements of these regulations. 


(3) No person, - 


(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or 
(b) who having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person. 


shall be eligible for appointment to any grade or post to which these regulations apply; 


Provided that the Central Government in case of appointment of Head of Departments and 
Chairperson in all other cases may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal law 
applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for so doing, 
exempt any person from the operation of this sub regulation. 


(4) No candidate who has been convicted by a Court of Law for an offence involving moral turpitude or 
who has been adjudged as an insolvent shall be eligible for appointment to a grade or post. 


(5) A candidate shall be in good mental and physical health and free from any physical defects which 
would not likely to interfere with the discharge of his duties as an employee of the Board and candidate, who 
after such medical examination as the Central Government in case of appointment of Head of Departments 
and Chairperson in all other cases may specify, is found not fit shall not be appointed in any grade or post. 


(6) If any question arises whether a candidate does or does not satisfy all or any of the requirements of 
this regulation, the same shall be decided by the Central Government in case of Head of Departments, and 
Chairperson in all other cases. 


9. Eligibility of existing employees for direct recruitment - The employees of the Board of any Major Port 
Authority possessing the prescribed qualifications and experience are eligible to apply for direct recruitment; provided 
that the age limit in such cases shall not exceed fifty-five years. 


10. Advertisement of vacancies - (1) The vacancies for Class-III and Class-IV posts to be filled by direct 
recruitment shall be notified to the local Employment Exchange and in case sufficient number of eligible and suitable 
candidates are not available, the vacancies shall be advertised in widely circulated newspapers published within the

13. Select list - The Services Selection Committee may recommend, in the order of merit, as adjudged by it, the 


names of the selected candidates to be kept on a select list for consideration of appointment to posts earmarked for 
direct recruits and such a list shall be deemed to be valid for a period of twelve months from the date on which the list 
is approved by the Appointing Authority and it is open to the Appointing Authority to extend the validity of the list for 
a period not exceeding six months or until a fresh select list is approved whichever is earlier. 


14. Consideration of recommendations of Services Selection Committee and adhoc appointments - All 
appointments by direct recruitment shall be made by the Appointing Authority on the recommendations of the 
concerned Services Selection Committee: 


Provided that it shall be open to the Appointing Authority for reasons to be recorded in writing, not to accept 
the recommendations of Services Selection Committee. 


Provided further that where the Appointing Authority is an authority subordinate to the Chairperson and the 
authority disagrees with such recommendations in any case, it shall record its reasons for such disagreement and submit 
the case to the Chairperson whose decision in the matter shall be final. 


Provided also that in the case of, a purely temporary post, a leave vacancy or a vacancy earmarked for direct 
recruitment requiring immediate filling up, the Chairperson may appoint a person who is eligible to fill the vacant post 
for a period of six months at a time and not exceeding one year on adhoc basis subject to the condition that: 


(a) ad-hoc appointment, where unavoidable, shall be made strictly subject to fulfilling the qualifications, 
experience provided under recruitment rules; 


(b) the total period of appointment to a temporary post shall not exceed the tenure of the post; 


(c) inother cases, the temporary appointment shall be replaced by a regular appointment from the select list 
as soon as possible. 


15. Disqualification for canvassing - Any endeavour on the part of a person to canvass support by direct or 
indirect method for appointment to a post or for promotion to a higher post shall disqualify for the appointment or 
promotion. 


16. False information to be treated as disqualification - Any candidate who is found to have knowingly 
furnished any particulars which are false or have suppressed material information of a character, which if known would 
ordinarily have debarred him from getting an appointment to a grade or post, is liable to be disqualified, and, if 
appointed, to be dismissed from service. 

17. Cancellation of appointment order - If a candidate selected for the post earmarked for direct recruits fails

to join duty within the date mentioned in the offer of appointment and where no such date is mentioned, within a period 
of thirty days of the date of issue of the offer of appointment or within such extended period as the Appointing Authority 
may agree, the offer of appointment shall be deemed to have been cancelled. 


18. Payment of travelling allowance for attending interview - A candidate appearing for written and practical 
tests or interviews shall bear his/her own expenses; 


Provided that the candidates belonging to the Scheduled Castes or the Scheduled Tribes called for written or 
trade tests or interview shall be paid travelling allowance equal to first class rail fare by shortest practicable route both 
ways on production of proof to the effect that he has actually performed the inward journey. 


19. Probation Period - (1) Every person appointed to a post of direct recruitment or promotion or absorption 
shall, subject to the provisions of sub-regulations (2) and (3), be on probation for a period of two years except in case 
of persons appointed on absorption basis through composite 'method of recruitment in the posts of Head of Departments 
and Deputy Head of Departments carrying the scales of pay of Rs. 80000-220000 and above: 


Provided that where the appointment itself is for a period specified in the appointment order, such appointment 
shall stand terminated on the expiry of such period, unless such period is extended by the appointing authority: 


Provided further that, when the appointment is made by the direct recruitment and the post carries a scale of 
pay, the maximum of which does not exceed Rs. 88,700/-, the period of probation shall be one year: 


Provided also that, there shall not be any probation in case of appointment by promotion within Class-III and 
Class-IV grades: 


Provided also that, if an employee, on probation to a grade or post is appointed to officiate in a higher grade 
or post, he shall be eligible to count the duration of his appointment to a higher grade or post to complete probation in 
his lower grade or post, and similarly, if an employee who has previously been appointed to officiate in a grade or post, 
he may on appointment to the similar grade or post on probation shall be eligible to count such officiating period 
(excluding Ad-hoc service) to complete probation in the grade or post. 


(2) The period of probation may, if the appointing authority deems fit, be extended for a specific period at a 
time, but the total period of such extensions shall not, save where any extension is necessary by reason of any 


departmental or legal proceedings pending against the employee, exceed one year. 


(3) During the period of his probation an employee may be required to undergo such departmental training and 
pass such departmental tests as the appointing authority may, from time to time, specify in this behalf. 


20. Confirmation of employee on probation - 


(1) General: 


(i) Confirmation shall be made only once in the service of an employee which shall be in the entry 
grade; 


(ii) Confirmation shall be delinked from the availability of permanent vacancy in the grade i.e. an 
officer who has successfully completed the probation period may be considered for 
confirmation. 

(2) Confirmation in the grade to which initially recruited - 
The appointee shall satisfactorily complete the probation and thereafter his case shall be placed 


before Departmental Promotion Committee (for confirmation) and on confirmation, an order of 
confirmation shall be issued when the case is cleared from all angles. 


(3) On Promotion - 


(1) If the recruitment rules do not prescribe any probation, an officer promoted on regular basis 
(after following the prescribed Departmental Promotion Committee, etc., procedure) shall have all the 


68 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4] 


benefits applicable to a person confirmed in that grade; 


(ii) where probation is prescribed, the appointing authority shall on completion of the 
prescribed period of probation assess the work and conduct of the officer himself and in case the 
conclusion is that the officer is fit to hold the higher grade, he will pass an order declaring that the 
person concerned has successfully completed the probation and the work of the officer has not been 
satisfactory or needs to be improved, he may revert him to the post or grade from which he was 
promoted, or extend the period of probation as the case may be. 


(iii) Since there will be no confirmation on promotion before an official is declared to have 
completed the probation satisfactorily, a rigorous screening of his performance shall be made and 
there shall be no hesitation to revert a person to the post or grade from which he was promoted if the 
work of the officer during probation has not been satisfactory. 


(2) Confirmation of probationers — (i) a person appointed against a permanent post as a direct recruit 

with definite conditions of probation shall be confirmed in the grade with effect from the date on 
which he successfully completed the period of probation. The decision whether he should be 
confirmed or his probation extended shall be taken soon after the expiry of the initial probation period, 
i.e., ordinarily within a period of six to eight weeks and communicated to the employee together with 
the reasons in case of extension. Even though the meetings of the Departmental Promotion Committee 
may be held after the termination of the period of probation of direct recruits, a person appointed 
against a permanent post with definite conditions of probation shall be confirmed in the grade with 
effect from the date on which he successfully completes the period of probation. A probationer who 
is not making satisfactory progress or who shown himself to be inadequate for the service shall be 
informed of his shortcomings well before the expiry of the original probationary period so that he can 
make severe efforts at self-improvement; 
(1) in the case of probation, the Departmental Promotion Committee shall not determine the relative 
grading of officers but only decide whether they should be declared to have completed the probation 
satisfactorily. If the performance of any probationer is not satisfactory, that Departmental Promotion 
Committee may advise whether the period of probation should be extended or whether he should be 
discharged from service. 


21. Discharge or reversion of employees on probation - (1) If an employee on probation in his first appointment 
is not considered fit, on the basis of his conduct or performance, for confirmation at the end of the period of probation 
prescribed in regulation 19, he shall be discharged from the service of the Board. 


(2) If an employee on probation who holds a lien on a post and does not complete the period of probation as 
specified under regulation 19 to the satisfaction of the appointing authority; he may be reverted to the post on which 
he holds a lien. 


(3) If an employee during the period of probation on a post is considered unfit for further retention in that post 
on the basis of performance or conduct or failure to pass the departmental test if prescribed, he shall be liable to be 
discharged from service at any time if he has no lien on any post or reverted to the post in which he holds a lien. 


22. Departmental test for Promotion, Confirmation in certain cases - (1) The Chairperson may specify, from 
time to time, the posts, confirmation in or promotion to which shall be subject to the passing of a qualifying 
departmental test, if any. 


(2) The Chairperson may also specify from time to time, the details of the qualifying departmental test such as the 
procedure for holding the test, the syllabus for the test, the intervals at which the test shall be held, the maximum period 
within which the test shall be passed by the candidates, etc. 


23. Reversion due to failure in departmental test - An employee promoted to a post shall pass such qualifying 
departmental test, if any, as may be specified by the Chairperson from time to time, within such period, as may be 
specified by him failing which the employee shall be reverted: 


Provided that when the passing of a test is specified as a condition precedent to promotion to a higher post, no 
employee shall be considered for promotion to such a post, until he passes the prescribed test.
