24. Seniority List - An up-to-date gradation list indicating the inter-se seniority of the employees shall be 
maintained for each grade and the list shall indicate separately the permanent and temporary employees in each grade, 
and shall be circulated every year. 


25. Fixation of seniority — (1) The seniority of persons directly recruited to a grade and persons appointed on the 
basis of departmental promotion shall be assigned inter se seniority according to rotation of vacancies between direct 
recruits and promotes which shall be based on the quota of vacancies in the grade reserved for direct recruitment and 
promotion as indicated in the Schedule and in cases where exchange of vacancies has been resorted to as per regulation 
6, the seniority shall be as per the mode of filling up. 


(2) The direct recruits shall be ranked inter-se in the order of merit in which they are placed in the select list on the 
basis of their performance in the examination or interview or both, the recruits of an earlier select list being ranked 
senior to those of a later select list. 


(3) The persons appointed against promotion quota of vacancies shall be ranked inter-se according to the order in 
which they are approved for promotion by the Departmental Promotion Committee. 


(4) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-regulations (1) to (3) above, the seniority already determined prior to 
the commencement of these regulations shall remain unaffected. 


26. Departmental Promotion Committee — (1) There shall be a Departmental Promotion Committee for each 
grade or post to recommend a panel of employees for appointment to different posts by promotion in accordance with 
these regulations. 


(2) The composition of the Departmental Promotion Committee shall be the same as that of the Services Selection 
Committee as laid down in regulation 12 and the validity of the panel shall be the same as mentioned in regulation 13. 


27. Field of selection for promotion - (1) Where one or more posts in a grade are required to be filled by 
promotion through selection method from employees holding posts in the feeder grade in accordance with the 
prescribed recruitment rules, the employees holding the eligible posts and having the prescribed qualifications and 
experience for promotion shall be considered for promotion if they fall within the zone of consideration. 


(2) The following procedure shall be observed while recommending employees for promotion through selection 
method, namely: - 


(a) the Departmental Promotion Committee (DPC) shall determine the merit of those being assessed for 
promotion with reference to the prescribed benchmark and accordingly grade the officers as 'fit' or 'unfit'. Only 
those who are graded 'fit' by the Departmental Promotion Committee shall be included and arranged in the 
select list in order of their inter se seniority in the feeder grade. Those Officers who are graded as 'unfit' by the 
Departmental Promotion Committee shall not be included in the select list. 


(b) the Departmental Promotion Committee shall also consider the cases of eligible employees who are on foreign 
service or on study leave. 


(c) the instructions issued by the Central Government from time to time on procedure to be followed in 
Departmental Promotion Committee proceedings in respect of Central Government servants shall mutatis 
mutandis apply. 


Note: - For absorption to the post carrying pay scale of Rs.80000-220000 and above and for which composite 
method of recruitment is adopted, the benchmark in the overall grading shall be "Very Good' and in all other 
cases, the benchmark shall be "Good". 


(3) For promotion to non- selection posts, where no bench mark is specified, the criteria for selection shall be 
seniority-cum-fitness. 


28. Adhoc appointments - In case of immediate necessity when a panel recommended by the Departmental 
Promotion Committee has been completed, the appointing authority may make a purely adhoc appointment to a 
post, by appointing the senior most eligible and suitable employee in the feeder grade or post up to a period of 
six months at a time and not exceeding one year or till a new panel is recommended by the Departmental

Compassionate appointments - 


Notwithstanding anything contained in these regulations, the Chairperson may dispense with the 
normal procedure of recruitment prescribed in these regulations and appoint to a Class-III or Class-IV post 
the legitimate son or daughter or the surviving spouse of an employee of the board, who dies while in service, 
subject to possessing the prescribed qualifications and experience and is otherwise found suitable. 


Interpretation - (1) In the application of these regulations all the instructions of the Central Government as 
amended from time to time which are not contrary to any of the provisions of these regulations and all 
instructions issued from time to time by the Central Government which cover matters not specifically covered 
will be followed. 


(2) Where a doubt arises as to the interpretation of any of the provisions these regulations, the matter shall be 
referred to the Chairperson for a decision whose decision thereon shall be final and binding.

MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS 
(RAILWAY BOARD) 
NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 6th November, 2026 


S.O. 600(E).— Whereas, by the notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of Railways (Railway 
Board), number G.S.R. 837(E), dated the | 90 November, 2025 published in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part I, 
Section 3, Sub — section (ii), dated the 2" November, 2025 and issued under sub-section () of section 20A of the 
Railways Act, 989 (24 of 989) (hereinafter referred to as the said Act), the Central Government declared its intention 
to acquire the land specified in the Schedule annexed to the said notification for the purpose of execution of the Special 
Railway Project, namely, 47 LINE BETWEEN BAREJADI - NANDEJ (GERATPUR) - SANAND (38.20 KM) 
IN THE DISTRICT OF AHMEDABAD in the State of Gujarat. 


And, whereas, the substance of the said notification has been published in the daily local news papers, namely, 
“The Times of India” (English), dated the 9" November, 2025, “Divya Bhaskar” (Gujarati) dated the 9" November, 
2025 and “Young Leader” (Hindi) dated the 9"" November 2025 under sub-section (4) of section 20A of the said Act; 


And, whereas, 26 (Twenty Six) numbers of objection have been received and the same have been considered 
and disallowed by the competent authority; 


And whereas, in pursuance of sub-section (l) of section 20E of the said Act, the competent authority has 
submitted its report to the Central Government. 


Now, therefore, upon receipt of the report of the Competent Authority and in exercise of the powers conferred 
by sub-section (/) of section 20E of the said Act, the Central Government hereby declares that the land specified in the 
Schedule annexed hereto shall be acquired for the aforesaid purpose. 


4 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


And further, in pursuance of sub-section (2) of section 20E of the said Act, the Central Government hereby 
declares that on publication of this notification in the Official Gazette, the land specified in the Schedule annexed 
hereto shall vest absolutely in the Central Government free from all encumbrances.

3. यह नीलामी भारतीय रिज़र्व बैंक, मुंबई कार्यालय, फोर्ट, मुंबई-400001 द्वारा 13 नवंबर 2026 को संचालित की

नवंबर 2026 को प्रस्तुत की जानी चाहिए। अप्रतिस्पर्धी बोलियां पूर्वाह्नन 10:30 बजे से पूर्वाह्न 11:00 बजे के बीच और 
प्रतिस्पर्धी बोलियां पूर्वाह्न 10:30 बजे से पूर्वाह्न 11:30 बजे के बीच प्रस्तुत की जानी चाहिए।

5. नीलामी का परिणाम भारतीय रिज़र्व बैंक द्वारा अपने वैबसाइट (www. rbi.org.in) पर 13 नवंबर 2026 को प्रदर्शित 
किया जाएगा। सफल बोलीदाताओं द्वारा भुगतान 16 नवंबर 2026 अर्थात्‌ पुनर्निर्गम की तारीख को किया जाएगा। 
प्रतिभूति के लिए भुगतान में नीलामी में आबंटित प्रतिभूति के अंकित मूल्य पर मूलनिर्गम/पिछले कूपन भुगतान की तारीख

Scheme for Non-competitive Bidding Facility in the Auction of 
Government of India Dated Securities and Treasury Bills 


I. Scope: With a view to encouraging wider participation and retail holding of Government securities, retail 
investors are allowed participation on “non-competitive” basis in select auctions of dated Government of 
India (Gol) securities and Treasury Bills. 


Il. Definitions: For the purpose of this scheme, the terms shall bear the meaning assigned to them as under: 


a. Retail investor is any person, including individuals, firms, companies, corporate bodies, institutions, 
provident funds, trusts, and any other entity as may be prescribed by RBI. 


b. ‘Aggregator/Facilitator’ means a Scheduled Bank or Primary Dealer or Specified Stock Exchange or 
any other entity approved by RBI, permitted to aggregate the bids received from the investors and 
submit a single bid in the non-competitive segment of the primary auction. 


c. ‘Specified stock exchange’ means SEBI recognized Stock Exchange, which have received No 
Objection Certificate (NOC) from SEBI to act as aggregator/facilitator in the primary auction 
segment. 


d. ‘Eligible Provident Funds’ are those non-government provident funds governed by the Provident 
Funds Act, 1925 whose investment pattern is decided by the Government of India. 


गा. Eligibility: 
a. Participation on a non-competitive basis in the auctions will be open to a retail investor who: 


1. Does not maintain current account (CA) or subsidiary General Ledger (SGL) account with the 
Reserve Bank of India; and 


2. Submits the bid indirectly through an Aggregator/Facilitator permitted under the scheme; or 
3. Maintains the ‘Retail Direct Gilt Account’ (RDG Account) with RBI 


Exceptions: 
a. Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) and Cooperative Banks: 


i. Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) and Cooperative Banks shall be covered under this Scheme only 
in the auctions of dated securities in view of their statutory obligations. 


ii. Since these banks maintain SGL account and current account with the Reserve Bank of India, 
they shall be eligible to submit their non-competitive bids directly. 


b. State Governments, eligible provident funds and Others: 


i. State Governments, eligible provident funds in India, the Nepal Rashtra Bank, Royal Monetary 
Authority of Bhutan and any Person or Institution, specified by the Bank, with the approval of 
Government, shall be covered under this scheme only in the auctions of Treasury Bills. 


ii. These bids will be outside the notified amount. 


iii. There will not be any restriction on the maximum amount of bid for these entities. 


IV. Quantum: Allocation of non-competitive bids from retail investors will be restricted to a maximum of 
five percent of the aggregate nominal amount of the issue within the notified amount as specified by the 
Government of India, or any other percentage determined by Reserve Bank of India. 


V. Amount of Bid: 


a. The minimum amount for bidding will be 10,000 (face value) and therefore in multiples in 710,000 
as hitherto. 


b. In the auctions of Gol dated securities, the retail investors can make a single bid for an amount not 
more than Rupees Two crore (face value) per security per auction. 


VI. Other Operational Guidelines: 


a. The retail investor desirous of participating in the auction under the Scheme would be required to 
maintain a depository account with any of the depositories or a gilt account under the constituent

(RDG Account) with RBI. 


Under the Scheme, an investor can make only a single bid in an auction. An undertaking to the

Aggregator/Facilitator.

९. 


Each Aggregator/Facilitator on the basis of firm orders received from their constituents with submit

Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (E-Kuber) system. Except in extraordinary 
circumstances such as general failure of the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (E- 
Kuber) system, non-competitive bid in physical form will not be accepted. 


Allotment of Bids: 


d. 


Allotment under the non-competitive segment to the Aggregator/Facilitator will be at the weighted 
average rate of yield/price that will emerge in the auction on the basis of the competitive bidding. 
The securities will be issued to the Aggregator/Facilitator against payment on the date of issue 
irrespective of whether they have received payment from their clients. 


In case the aggregate amount of bid is more than the reserved amount (5% of notified amount), pro 
rata allotment would be made. In case of partial allotments, it will be the responsibility of the 
Aggregator/Facilitator to appropriately allocate securities to their clients in a transparent manner. 


In case the aggregate amount of bids is less than the reserved amount, the shortfall will be taken to 
competitive portion. 


Issue of Security: 


g.. 


Security would be issued only in SGL form by RBI. The Aggregator/Facilitator has to clearly 
indicate at the time of tendering the non-competitive bids the amounts (face value) to be credited to 
their main SGL or CSGL account. 


Delivery in physical form from the Main SGL account is permissible at the instance of the investor

It will be the responsibility of the Aggregator/Facilitator to pass on the securities to their clients. 
Except in extraordinary circumstances, the transfer of securities to the client should b completed 
within five working days from the date of issue.

and may, after hearing all such objections and after making such further inquiry, if any, as the competent authority 
thinks necessary, by order, either allow or disallow the objections. 


Any order made by the competent authority under sub-section (2) of 20D of the said Act shall be final.

NOTIFICATION 
Mumbai, the 3rd November, 2026 
Under clause 20A of the Railways Act, 1989 (24 of 1989) 


S.O. 6106(E).— In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (1) of Section 20A of the Railways Act, 
1989 (24 of 1989) (hereinafter referred to as the said Act), the Central Government, after being satisfied that for the 
public purpose, the land, the brief description of which has been given in schedule annexed hereto, is required for 
purpose of execution, maintenance, management and operation of Special Railway Project, namely “Miraj Chord line 
Project (1.73 Km)” in the Sangli district of the State of Maharashtra, hereby declares its intention to acquire the said 
land. 


Any person interested in the said land may, within thirty days from the date of publication of this notification 
in the Official Gazette, file an objection regarding the acquisition and use of such land for the aforementioned purpose, 
in accordance with sub-section (1) of Section 20D of the said Act.

Every such objection shall be submitted in writing to the Competent Authority—namely, the Deputy 
Collector, Land acquisition no.7, Sangli, located on the Sangli-Miraj Road, Vijaynagar, Sangli, District Sangli, 
Maharashtra—and shall specify the grounds for the objection. The Competent Authority shall provide the objector an 
opportunity to be heard, either in person or through a legal practitioner. After hearing such objections and conducting 
such inquiries as the Competent Authority may deem necessary, the Authority shall, by an order, either allow or disallow 
the objections. 


Any order passed by the Competent Authority under sub-section (2) of Section 20D of the said Act shall be 
final. 


The land plans and other details of the land covered under this notification are available and can be inspected 
by the interested person at the aforesaid office of the Competent Authority.

एलेमाई ने प्राधिकारी के समक्ष अभ्यावेदन प्रस्तुत किए हैं कि भारत में घरेलू उद्योग को देश में पाटित आयातों के

पहले सेतु पोर्टल के माध्यम से प्रस्तुत किया जाना चाहिए। इसके बाद प्राप्त अनुरोधों पर विचार नहीं किया जाएगा। 


ड. गोपनीय आधार पर सूचना प्रस्तुत करता 


यदि वर्तमान जांच का कोई पक्षकार प्राधिकारी के समक्ष गोपनीय प्रस्तुति देता है या गोपनीय आधार पर सूचना 
उपलब्ध कराता है, तो उसे नियमावली के नियम 7(2) तथा इस संबंध में प्राधिकारी द्वारा जारी संबंधित व्यापार 
सूचनाओं के अनुसार ऐसी जानकारी का गैर-गोपनीय संस्करण भी साथ ही प्रस्तुत करना होगा। उक्त आवश्यकता का 
पालन न किए जाने पर प्रश्नावली के उत्तर/प्रस्तुतियां अस्वीकार की जा सकती हैं। 


प्राधिकारी के समक्ष प्रश्नावली के उत्तरों सहित कोई भी प्रस्तुति (इसके साथ संलग्न परिशिष्टों/अनुबंधों सहित) देने 
वाले पक्षकारों को गोपनीय और गैर-गोपनीय संस्करण अलग-अलग दाखिल करने होंगे। 


ऐसी प्रत्येक प्रस्तुति के प्रत्येक पृष्ठ के शीर्ष पर स्पष्ट रूप से 'गोपनीय' अथवा 'गैर-गोपनीय' अंकित होना चाहिए। इस 
प्रकार का अंकन किए बिना प्राधिकारी के समक्ष प्रस्तुत किसी भी सामग्री को प्राधिकारी गैर-गोपनीय सूचना मानेगा 
तथा अन्य इच्छुक पक्षकारों को उसका निरीक्षण करने की अनुमति देने के लिए स्वतंत्र होगा। 


गोपनीय संस्करण में वह समस्त जानकारी शामिल होनी चाहिए जो अपनी प्रकृति से गोपनीय है और/अथवा ऐसी 
अन्य जानकारी जिसे उपलब्ध कराने वाला पक्षकार गोपनीय होने का दावा करता Sl स्वभावतः गोपनीय या अन्य 
कारणों से गोपनीय होने का दावा की गई जानकारी के संबंध में उस जानकारी को उपलब्ध कराने वाले पक्षकार को 
उचित कारण दर्शाने वाला विवरण भी देना होगा, जिसमें स्पष्ट किया जाए कि ऐसी जानकारी प्रकट क्‍यों नहीं की 
जा सकती। 


इच्छुक पक्षकारों द्वारा दाखिल जानकारी का गैर-गोपनीय संस्करण गोपनीय संस्करण की प्रतिकृति होना चाहिए, 
जिसमें गोपनीय जानकारी को अधिमानतः सूचकांकित किया जाए अथवा (जहां सूचकांकीकरण संभव न हो) रिक्त 
रखा जाए। गोपनीयता का दावा की गई जानकारी की प्रकृति के अनुसार उसका उपयुक्त और पर्याप्त सारांश भी 
दिया जाना चाहिए। 


गैर-गोपनीय सारांश इतना विस्तृत होना चाहिए कि गोपनीय आधार पर प्रस्तुत जानकारी के सार को उचित रूप से 
समझा जा सके। तथापि, असाधारण परिस्थितियों में गोपनीय जानकारी प्रस्तुत करने वाला पक्षकार यह बता सकता 
है कि ऐसी जानकारी का सारांश बनाना संभव नहीं है। ऐसे मामले में नियमावली के नियम 7 और प्राधिकारी द्वारा 
जारी संबंधित व्यापार सूचनाओं के अनुसार, सारांश प्रस्तुत करना FAT संभव नहीं है, इसका पर्याप्त और समुचित 
स्पष्टीकरण सहित कारणों का विवरण प्राधिकारी की संतुष्टि के लिए प्रस्तुत करना होगा। 


इच्छुक पक्षकार दस्तावेजों के गैर-गोपनीय संस्करण के परिसंचरण की तारीख से 7 दिनों के भीतर गोपनीयता 
संबंधी मुद्दों पर अपनी टिप्पणियां प्रस्तुत कर सकते हैं। 


कोई भी प्रस्तुति, जिसका सार्थक गैर-गोपनीय संस्करण उपलब्ध नहीं कराया गया है अथवा जिसके गोपनीयता के 
दावे के संबंध में नियमावली के नियम 7 तथा प्राधिकारी द्वारा जारी संबंधित व्यापार सूचनाओं के अनुसार पर्याप्त 
और समुचित उचित-कारण विवरण नहीं दिया गया है, प्राधिकारी द्वारा अभिलेख पर नहीं ली जाएगी। 


प्राधिकारी प्रस्तुत जानकारी की प्रकृति की जांच करके गोपनीयता संबंधी अनुरोध को स्वीकार अथवा अस्वीकार कर 
सकता है। यदि प्राधिकारी संतुष्ट है कि गोपनीयता का अनुरोध उचित नहीं है अथवा जानकारी उपलब्ध कराने वाला 
पक्षकार उसे सार्वजनिक करने या सामान्यीकृत रूप अथवा सारांश के रूप में प्रकट करने की अनुमति देने के लिए 
तैयार नहीं है, तो प्राधिकारी ऐसी जानकारी की उपेक्षा कर सकता है।

A. Background 


F. No. 6/67/2026-DGTR.—Having regard to the Customs Tariff Act, 1975, as amended from time to time 
(hereinafter referred to as the ‘Act’) and the Customs Tariff (Identification, Assessment and Collection of Anti- 
Dumping Duty on Dumped Articles and for Determination of Injury) Rules, 1995, as amended from time to time 
(hereinafter referred to as the ‘AD Rules, 1995’ or the ‘Rules’), representations have been received by the Designated 
Authority (hereinafter referred to as the ‘Authority’) from the Aluminium Extrusion Manufacturers Association of 
India (hereinafter referred to as ‘ALEMAI’ or the ‘Association’), representing 228 manufacturers of “Aluminium 
Extrusion Profiles, Structures and Articles thereof” (hereinafter referred to as the ‘product under consideration’ or the 
‘subject goods’ or the ‘PUC’). ALEMAT has stated that the domestic industry is suffering injury on account of a 
significant increase in the dumped imports of the subject goods from China PR, Malaysia, Vietnam and Thailand 
(hereinafter referred to as subject countries). 


1. Nine domestic producers, who are members of ALEMAI, have also filed representations seeking imposition of 
ADD. These companies have furnished their financial statements Additionally, vide letters dated 4" November 
2026, 3 domestic producers who are members of ALEMAI have submitted summary cost information, and 
estimates of dumping and injury margin in respect of imports from the subject countries.

ALEMAT has submitted that most of its members are small units in the MSME category, and has requested the

Rule 5(4) of the Rules provides as under: 
“(4) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-rule (1) the designated authority may initiate an 
investigation suo motu if it is satisfied from the information received from the Principal Commissioner of 
Customs or Commissioner of Customs, as the case may be, appointed under the Customs Act, 1962 (52 of 
1962) or from any other source that sufficient evidence exists as to the existence of the circumstances 
referred to in clause (b) of sub-rule (3).” 


The Authority, accordingly, takes cognizance of the information provided by ALEMAI and its member 
producers and the import data available on record, in terms of Rule 5(4) of the Rules, for the purpose of 
examining whether sufficient evidence exists as to the existence of dumping, injury and causal link, as referred 
to in Rule 5(3)(b) of the Rules. 


B. Product under consideration 


The product under consideration in the present investigation is “Aluminium Extrusion Profiles, Structures and 
Articles thereof’. The subject goods may be alloyed or non-alloyed and are produced by the extrusion process 
in the form of profiles (solid, hollow or semi-hollow), bars, rods, tubes and pipes. 


The subject goods are sold either in mill finish or surface treated (anodized, powder coated, liquid painted, 
electrophoretically coated, wood-grain or sublimation finished, polished or brushed). The goods may be sold as 
such, or further fabricated (i.e., cut to length, drilled, punched, notched, mitred, bent, welded, machined or 
threaded), and are used to make structures and articles for eventual end consumption. 


Accordingly, the scope of the product under consideration includes the following: 

(a) Extruded profiles for architectural, industrial, transport, electrical and general engineering applications; 

(b) Extruded bars and rods, other than wire rods; 

(c) Extruded seamed or seamless tubes and pipes, whether or not subsequently drawn; 

(d) Doors, windows and their frames and thresholds, curtain-wall and fagade systems, partitions, louvres, 
railings and balustrades, and other structures and parts of structures made from aluminium extrusions, as well 
as profiles, tubes and the like prepared for use in structures; and 

(e) Other articles made predominantly from aluminium extrusions, such as heat sinks, LED and lighting 
profiles, industrial framing (T-slot) profiles, solar mounting structures, ladders and furniture, kitchen and 
wardrobe profiles, bicycle parts and formwork. 


ALEMAT has submitted that profiles, bars, rods, tubes, structures and articles made through the extrusion 
process are different variants of a single product, since (a) all forms are produced from aluminium billet, cast 
from primary aluminium ingot and/or aluminium scrap with the required alloying material; (b) all forms are 
produced on the same hydraulic extrusion press, through the same stages of billet heating, extrusion, 
quenching, stretching, cutting and ageing, the only difference between a hollow and a solid profile being the 
die; (c) structures and articles are made from extruded profiles only by cutting, machining, welding or joining, 
and the extruded profile gives the finished structure or article its essential character and accounts for the 
predominant part of its cost; and (d) the output at each stage (profile, structure or article) is capable of being 
sold as such.

The Authority prima facie notes that the structures and articles included in the scope are made from extruded

The product under consideration is used in a wide range of architectural, industrial, transport, electrical and 
general engineering applications, such as windows, doors, curtain-wall and facade systems, partitions, railings, 
heat sinks and lighting profiles, industrial framing, solar mounting structures, ladders, furniture, kitchen and 
wardrobe profiles, bicycle parts and formwork. 


The main raw material is aluminium billet, made by melting primary aluminium and/or aluminium scrap and 
adding small quantities of other metals to obtain the required alloy. The billet is cut to length, heated to about 
450-500°C and pushed by a hydraulic ram through a die. The extruded profile is cooled, stretched, cut to 
standard lengths and aged in an oven to attain the required hardness and strength (such as T5 or T6 temper). 
The profiles may thereafter be anodised, powder coated or otherwise finished, and may be cut, drilled, 
punched, machined, welded or joined to make structures and articles.

D. Domestic industry and standing 


The Authority notes that the Indian industry producing the subject goods is fragmented in nature and comprises 
largely of units in the MSME category. ALEMAIT represents 228 manufacturers of the subject goods in India. 
The Authority is prima facie satisfied that the representation has been made by or on behalf of the domestic 
industry in terms of the provisions contained in Rule 2(b) and Rule 5(3) of the Rules. 


Considering the MSME and fragmented nature of the industry and the number of producers involved, the 
Authority, in terms of Trade Notice 09/2021 dated 297 July 2021, seeks information from the domestic 
producers as per Annexure I referred to in the said trade notice. Based on the information so received, the 
Authority shall determine the scope of the domestic industry within the meaning of Rule 2(b) of the Rules and 
shall undertake sampling of domestic producers for the purpose of determination of injury margin. Therefore, 
while the information concerning all producers constituting the domestic industry will be considered for injury 
analysis, the non-injurious price and injury margin will be determined based on the data of the sampled 
producers. 


E. Subject countries 


The subject countries in the present investigation are China PR, Malaysia, Vietnam and Thailand (hereinafter 
referred to as the ‘subject countries’). 


F. Period of investigation 


The period of investigation (‘POI’) for the present investigation is Ist April 2025 to 30th June 2026 (15 
months). The injury investigation period shall cover the periods Ist April 2022 to 31st March 2023, Ist April 
2023 to 31st March 2024, Ist April 2024 to 31st March 2025 and the POI. 


Rule 5(3A) of the Rules provides that the period of investigation shall not be more than six months old as on 
the date of initiation, and shall normally be twelve months, while for reasons to be recorded in writing the 
Authority may consider a minimum of six months or a maximum of eighteen months. In the present case, the 
domestic producers are predominantly MSME units which maintain their records on a financial-year basis. 
Adoption of a twelve-month period from July 2025 to June 2026 would have resulted in substantial practical 
difficulties in the preparation and verification of information by such producers. Inclusion of the complete 
financial year 2025-26 within the POI is, therefore, considered appropriate, and is not expected to skew the 
data. Accordingly, a period of investigation of fifteen months has been adopted in the present case.

H. Basis of alleged injury 


ALEMAT has made representations before the Authority that the domestic industry in India has suffered injury 
due to the dumped imports into the country. The volume of the subject imports from the subject countries has 
increased significantly in absolute terms. Available information also indicates that the industry has suffered 
injury as the dumped imports were undercutting the prices of the industry, resulting in significant decline in 
profitability, and it is suffering losses. The industry is also facing decline in cash profits and return on capital 
employed. The industry is also facing significant underutilization of production capacities. While complete 
information on the impact on economic parameters is not available with the Authority at this stage, it is 
nonetheless prima facie observed based on information received that the domestic industry has suffered injury 
due to dumped imports.

its member producers and the import data available on record, that sufficient evidence exists as to the dumping 
of the product under consideration originating in or exported from the subject countries, the consequent 
material injury to the domestic industry and the causal link between such injury and the dumped imports, as 
referred to in Rule 5(3)(b) of the Rules, the Authority, in accordance with Section 9A of the Act read with Rule 
5(4) of the Rules, hereby suo motu initiates an anti-dumping investigation to determine the existence, degree 
and effect of the alleged dumping in respect of the product under consideration originating in or exported from 
the subject countries, and to recommend the amount of anti-dumping duty which, if levied, would be adequate 
to remove the injury to the domestic industry.

including questionnaire responses, are required to file confidential and non-confidential versions separately. 


Such submissions must be clearly marked as ‘confidential’ or ‘non-confidential’ at the top of each page. Any 
submission that has been made to the Authority without such markings shall be treated as ‘non-confidential’ 
information by the Authority, and the Authority shall be at liberty to allow other interested parties to inspect 
such submissions. 


The confidential version shall contain all information which is, by nature, confidential and/or other information 
which the supplier of such information claims as confidential. For the information which is claimed to be 
confidential by nature, or the information on which confidentiality is claimed for other reasons, the supplier of 
the information is required to provide a good cause statement along with the supplied information as to why

confidential version, with the confidential information preferably indexed or blanked out (where indexation is 
not possible), and such information must be appropriately and adequately summarized depending upon the 
information on which confidentiality is claimed.

substance of the information furnished on a confidential basis. However, in exceptional circumstances, the 
party submitting the confidential information may indicate that such information is not susceptible to summary, 
and a statement of reasons containing a sufficient and adequate explanation, in terms of Rule 7 of the Rules and

तीन प्रतिशत के बराबर राशि का भुगतान न्यास को करेगा। 

4. केंद्र सरकार द्वारा एनएमईडीटी कोष की राशि संबंधित राज्य सरकारों से प्राप्त की जाएगी, जो खनिकों से इसे एकत्र 
करेगी। 

ख. कोष का प्रशासन 

कोष के प्रशासन के लिए नोडल मंत्रालय खान मंत्रालय होगा। राज्य सरकारों को खान मंत्रालय द्वारा निर्धारित एमआईएस 
(इलेक्ट्रॉनिक रूप से) के माध्यम से प्रत्येक माह या तिमाही में कोष में हुई वृद्धि और बजट तैयार करने के लिए कोई अन्य 
अतिरिक्त जानकारी की रिपोर्ट देनी होगी। 

ग. कोष में वृद्धि 


दूसरी अनुसूची के अनुसार भुगतान की गई रॉयल्टी के तीन प्रतिशत के बराबर राशि एनएमईडीटी कोष में जमा की जाएगी। 

राज्य सरकारों द्वारा इस तरह एकत्रित की गई राशि को शुरू में राज्य के लोक खाते में एक शीर्ष के तहत दर्ज किया जाएगा 

और उसके बाद इसे केंद्र को हस्तांतरित किया जाएगा। इन प्राप्तियों को खान मंत्रालय द्वारा भारत की समेकित कोष के तहत 
राजस्व प्राप्तियों के रूप में वर्गीकृत किया जाएगा और उसके बाद वर्ष के दौरान विनियोजनों के माध्यम से भारत के लोक 
लेखा खाते के तहत एनएमईडीटी कोष में समय-समय पर अंतरित किया जाएगा। 

जबकि एक वर्ष में संपूर्ण संचय को वित्त वर्ष के समापन से पहले अंतरित कर दिया जाना चाहिए, प्रत्येक माह प्रगतिशील 

संचय को अधिमानतः अंतरित किया जाना चाहिए। अंतर-खाता अंतरण के लिए उपयुक्त बजट प्रावधान तैयार किए जा सकते 

हैं।

हैं, को प्राप्त करने के लिए शासी निकाय द्वारा आवश्यक समझी जा सकते हैं:

2. एनएमईडीटी कोष से वित्त पोषित की जाने वाली समर्पित स्कीमों/कार्यकलापों को कोष को अधिसूचित करते समय उपयुक्त 


रूप से शामिल किया जाएगा। भारत के समेकित कोष में उक्त स्कीमों/कार्यकलापों के अंतर्गत व्यय के बजट प्रावधानों का उक्त

करते समय यह सुनिश्चित किया जा सकता है कि उक्त कोष में पर्याप्त शेष राशि है।

New Delhi, the 110 November, 2026 


Subject: Accounting Procedure of National Mineral Exploration and Development Trust 


99.0. 6149(E).— I. A. Establishment of Fund 1. In exercise of the power conferred by sub section (1) of 
section 9C of Mines & Mineral (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957 as amended on 26th March 2015, the Central 
Government has established a Trust namely National Mineral Exploration Trust with the objective of augmenting 
mineral exploration in the country. 


Accordingly, the Central Government decided to establish a Fund to be called National Mineral Exploration 
Trust (NMET) Fund. 


Further, as amended by Mines & Mineral (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2025, name of 
National Mineral Exploration Trust has been changed to National Mineral Exploration and Development Trust. 
Therefore, the name of NMET Fund will also be changed to National Mineral Exploration and Development Trust 
(NMEDT) Fund. 


2. The proposed fund shall be non-iapsable and placed under non-interest-bearing section of Public Account of India 
and shall be administered by Ministry of Mines. 


3. As per Section 9C (4) of Mines & Mineral (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2025, the holder of a 
mining lease or a composite license shall pay to the Trust a sum equivalent to three percent of the royalty paid in terms 
of the second schedule, in such manner as may be prescribed by the Central Government. 


4. The amount towards NMEDT Fund will be received by the Central Government from respective State Governments, 
which will collect the same from miners. 


B. Administration of the Fund 


The nodal ministry for administration of the Fund shall be Ministry of Mines. The State Governments shall be required 
to report the accretions each month / quarter through an MIS (electronically) as prescribed by Ministry of Mines and 
any other additional information for budget formulation for the fund. 


C. Accretions to the Fund 


A sum equivalent to three percent of the royalty paid in terms of second schedule shall be credited to NMEDT Fund. 
The sum so collected by State Governments shall initially be booked under a head in Public Account of State and 
thereafter transferred to the Centre. The receipts will be classified as revenue receipts under Consolidated Fund of India 
by Ministry of Mines and thereafter be periodically transferred to the NMEDT Fund under Public Account of India 
through appropriations during the year. 


While the entire accretion in a year should be transferred before close of the financial year, each month the progressive 
accretion should have been transferred preferably. Suitable budget provisions for the inter-account transfer may be 
formulated. 


D. Utilization of the fund 


1. The amount under this fund shall be utilised by the Trust to carry out regional and detailed exploration for minerals 
within India including the offshore areas, and outside India for the purposes of regional and detailed exploration and 
development of mines and minerals and it shall undertake such activities as may be deemed necessary by the Governing 
Body to achieve its objects, including, but not limited to: - 


(a) funding special studies and projects designed to identify, explore, extract, beneficiate, refine, critical and strategic 
minerals or deep-seated or concealed mineral deposits; 


(b) undertaking studies for mineral development, sustainable mining adoption of advanced scientific and 
technological practices and mineral extraction metallurgy; 


(c) taking up exploration of areas for regional and detailed exploration, giving priority particularly to strategic and 
critical minerals; 


(d) consulting Central Geological Programming Board to decide the priorities for exploration by the Trust; 


(e) facilitating exploration activities in such a manner that areas explored can be taken up for grant of mineral 
concessions in accordance with the provisions of the Act and the rules made thereunder;

(f) facilitating completion of brownfield regional exploration projects in obvious geological potential areas (G3) 
including conducting high-risk exploration for deep-seated mineral deposits through modern technologies; 


(g) promoting completion of detailed exploration (G2 or GI) in the areas where G3 stage exploration has been 
completed; 


(h) facilitating geophysical, ground and aerial, survey and geochemical survey of obvious geological potential areas; 


(i) facilitating a national core repository for encouraging research in earth sciences and for evaluation of the mineral 
prospects; 


() organizing capacity building programmes to raise technical capability of personnel engaged in or to be engaged 
in exploration; 


(k) | supporting and funding the objectives and schemes of the National Critical Mineral Mission, including domestic 
critical mineral exploration, support of exploration activities outside India, risk coverage of foreign sourcing and 
mineral recovery; 


(1) supporting and funding of mining, processing, beneficiation, evacuation infrastructure, technology upgradation 
and other activities related to mine development; and 


(m) using the Trust Fund for such other purposes that the Governing Body may decide, or authorise the Executive 
Committee to be necessary or expedient in the interest of conservation, development and exploitation of mineral 
resources of India, not inconsistent with the provisions of the Act. 


2. The dedicated schemes/activities to be funded from the NMEDT Fund shall be suitably included while notifying the 
Fund. The budget provisions for expenditure under said schemes/activities in the Consolidated Fund of India should be 
matched by recoupment from the said Fund. It may be ensured while making budget provisions for the earmarked 
schemes/ activities from NMEDT fund that there is a sufficient balance in the said Fund. 


E. Maintenance of Accounting records and the Broadsheet of NUEDT Fund 


1. Pay and Accounts Office, M/o Mines will maintain a broadsheet of accretions to and payments from the NMEDT 
fund and effect reconciliation on monthly basis thereof with the concerned Division. It should be ensured that there are 
no adverse balances under the Reserve Fund at any moment of time. Principal Accounts Officer shall provide inputs for 
budget formulation. 


2. The Appropriation Accounts of Mines shall reflect a synopsis of the transactions / flows and balances in the fund 
together with scheme wise utilization. 


F. Audit of NMEDT Fund 
The Accounts of NMEDT fund shall be subject to statutory audit by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India. The 
Accounts shall also be subject to audit by Internal Audit Wing of the O/o Chief Controller of Accounts, M/o Mines.

notification in the Official Gazette, raise objection to the acquisition and use of such land for the aforesaid purpose 
under sub-section(I) of section 20D of the said Act:

or by legal practitioner and may. After hearing all such objections and after making such further enquiry, if any as the 
competent authority thinks necessary, by order, either allow or disallow the objections. 


Any order made by the competent authority under sub-section (II) of section 20(D) of the said act shall be final.

interested person at the aforesaid office of the competent authority

NOTIFICATION 
Secunderabad, the 9th November, 2026 


S.O. 6181(E).— Whereas, by the notification by Government of India, in the Ministry of Railways (Railway 
Board), number S.O.No.3646 (E). Dated.03.07.2026 Published in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part-I Section 3 
Sub section (1), dated. 04.07.2026 (herein after referred to as said notification) and issued under sub section (1) of 
section 20(A) of the Railway Act, 1989 (24 of 1989), the Central Government declares its intention to acquire the land 
specified in the schedule annexed to the said notification for the Construction of Road Over Bridge in Lieu of Level 
Crossing (LC) No.250 at Km. 607/1-4 in between Bolaram — Cavalry Barracks stations in Machabollaram Village of 
Alwal Mandal in Medchal Malkajgiri District in the State of Telangana. 


And whereas an extract of this notification was published in the daily newspapers The Times of India, Sakshi 
Daily and V6Velugu Newspapers on 09 July, 2026 with the approval of Manoj Kumar, Chief Engineer, Construction, 
Road Safety Projects, South Central Railway, Secunderabad, under sub -section (1) Section 20A of this Act. 


And whereas the Competent Authority for Land Acquisition (CALA) and Revenue Divisional 
Officer, Malkajgiri has reported that no objections have been received from any person interested in the land at 
Machabollaram Village, Alwal Mandal, Medchal—Malkajgiri District, Telangana State, within the stipulated statutory 
period of thirty days as prescribed under Section 20D of the said Act. 


And whereas, in pursuance of sub-section (1) of 20(E) of this Act, the Competent Authority has submitted its 
report to the Central Government. 


Now, therefore, on receipt of the report of the Competent Authority for Land Acquisition (CALA) and in 
exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (1) of Section 20E of the said Act, the Central Government hereby 
declares that the lands mentioned in the Schedule hereto shall be acquired for the purpose mentioned above. 


Further, in pursuance of sub-section (2) of section 20E of this Act, the Central Government hereby declares on 
publication of notification in the Official Gazette, that the land specified in the schedule annexed here to shall vest 
absolutely in the Central Government is free from all encumbrances.

डिवीजन, पश्चिमी रेलवे" के निष्पादन के लिए आवश्यक है, Urge ऐसी भूमि के अधिग्रहण करने के अपने इरादे की घोषणा 
करती है। 

उक्त भूमि में रुचि रखने वाला कोई भी व्यक्ति, आधिकारिक राजपत्र में इस अधिसूचना के प्रकाशन की तारीख से 
तीस दिनों की अवधि के भीतर, उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 20डी की उपधारा (I) के तहत उपरोक्त उद्देश्य के लिए ऐसी भूमि 
के अधिग्रहण और उपयोग पर आपत्ति उठा सकता है। 

ऐसी प्रत्येक आपत्ति सक्षम प्राधिकारी, अर्थात डिप्टी कलेक्टर और प्रांत अधिकारी लिमखेड़ा, तालुका लिमखेड़ा,

NOTIFICATION 
Mumbai, the 12th November, 2026 
G.S.R. 982(E).— In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section(1) of section 20A of the Railways Act, 
1989 (24 of 1989) (here in after referred in as the said act 2008), the Central Government after being satisfied that for 
the public purpose, the land, the brief description of which has given in the schedule annexed here to, is required for 
execution of the Special Railway Project, namely, “Wadodara - Ratlam 3rd and 4th line (258.94 Km) Project of 
Ratlam Division on Western Railway” in District-DAHOD in the State of Gujarat, hereby declares its intention 


to acquired such land : 


Any person interested in the said land may, within a period of thirty days from the date of publication of 
this notification in the Official Gazette, raise objection to the acquisition and use of such land for the aforesaid purpose 


under sub-section(I) of section 20D of the said Act: 


Every such objection shall be made to the competent authority, namely, Deputy Collector and Prant 
officer Limkheda, Taluka Limkheda, District Dahod (Gujarat), in writing and shall set out the grounds thereof, 
and the competent authority shall give the objector an opportunity of being heard, either in person or by legal 
practitioner and May. After hearing all such objections and after making such further enquiry, if any as the competent 


authority thinks necessary, by order, either allow or disallow the objections. 


Any order made by the competent authority under sub-section (II) of section 20(D) of the said act shall be 
final. 


The land plans and other details of the land covered under this notification are available and can be inspected 


by the interested person at the aforesaid office of the competent authority.

MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS 
(South East Central Railway) 
NOTIFICATION 
Bilaspur, the 7th November, 2026 

S.O. 676(E).— In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (l) of section 20A of the Railways Act, 
989 (Railways Amendment Act, 2008), the Central Government, after being satisfied that for a public purpose, the 
land, the brief description of which is given in the Schedule below, is required for the execution, maintenance, 
management, and operation of a Special Railway Project, namely the construction of the Dongargarh — Gondia Fourth 
Railway Line (84.l0 km) in the States of Chhattisgarh and Maharashtra, hereby declares its intention to acquire such 
land, with or without structures thereon, in the villages described in the schedule under the Dongargarh and Lal Bahadur 


Nagar Tehsils of Rajnandgaon District in the State of Chhattisgarh. 


Any person interested in the said land may, within a period of thirty (30) days from the date of publication of 
this notification in the Official Gazette, object to the acquisition of such land for the aforementioned purpose under sub- 
section (l) of section 20D of the said Act. Every such objection shall be made in writing to the Competent Authority 
and Sub-Divisional Officer (Revenue), Dongargarh, District Rajnandgaon (Chhattisgarh), and shall set forth the grounds 
thereof. The Competent Authority shall provide the objector an opportunity of being heard, either in person or through 
a legal practitioner (Advocate), and after hearing all such objections and making such further inquiry, if any, as the 


Competent Authority thinks necessary, may, by order, either allow or disallow the objections. 


Any order made by the Competent Authority under sub-section (2) of section 20D of the said Act shall be 


final. 


The plans and other details of the land covered under this notification are available and can be inspected by 


the interested persons at the aforementioned office of the Competent Authority on any working day.

यह अनुज्ञप्ति परिसर के उस भाग में प्रमुखता से प्रदर्शित की जाएगी जो जनता के लिए खुला हो। 
अनुज्ञप्तिधारी उस समय प्रवृत्त औषध और प्रसाधन सामग्री अधिनियम, 1940 और उसके अंतर्गत नियमों के 


प्रावधानों का अनुपालन करेगा। 

थोक ATA को उसी अक्षुण्ण कंटेनर में बेचा जाना चाहिए जैसा कि निर्माता द्वारा आपूर्ति की गई है। 

यदि अनुज्ञप्तिधारी अनुज्ञप्ति की अवधि के दौरान अनुसूची सी, सी(1) और अनुसूची एक्स में सूचीबद्ध औषधों की अतिरिक्त 
श्रेणियों को बेचना, स्टॉक करना और बिक्री के लिए प्रदर्शित करना या वितरित करना चाहता है जो इस अनुज्ञप्ति में शामिल 
नहीं हैं, तो उसे आवश्यक अनुमति के लिए अनुज्ञप्ति प्राधिकारी को आवेदन करना ASU यह अनुज्ञप्ति उन औषधों की 
श्रेणियों तक विस्तारित मानी जाएगी जिनके संबंध में ऐसी अनुमति दी गई है। यह अनुमति अनुज्ञप्ति प्राधिकारी द्वारा अनुज्ञप्ति 
पर पृष्ठांकित की जाएगी।

अनुज्ञप्ति प्राप्त डीलर या विधिवत अनुन्ञप्ति प्राप्त निर्माता से नकद या क्रेडिट HAT के तहत न खरीदी गई हो। 
किसी भी थोक औषध (सक्रिय या निष्क्रिय थोक पदार्थ) की बिक्री पुनर्विक्रय के उद्देश्यों के लिए ऐसे व्यक्ति को नहीं की 
जाएगी जिसके पास थोक औषध (सक्रिय या निष्क्रिय थोक पदार्थ) को बेचने, स्टॉक करने या बिक्री के लिए प्रदर्शित 
करने या वितरित करने के लिए अपेक्षित अनुज्ञप्ति न हो: 
औषध निर्माण में उपयोग की जाने वाली किसी भी थोक औषध (सक्रिय या निष्क्रिय थोक पदार्थ) की बिक्री ऐसे व्यक्ति 
को नहीं की जाएगी जिसके पास अपेक्षित विनिर्माण अनुज्ञप्ति न हो। 
परंतु यह शर्त निम्नलिखित को किसी भी थोक औषध (सक्रिय या निष्क्रिय थोक पदार्थ) की बिक्री पर लागू नहीं होगी - 
सरकार की ओर से खरीद करने वाला कोई अधिकारी या प्राधिकारी, या 
अनुसंधान के उद्देश्य से शैक्षिक या अनुसंधान संस्थान 
हाइड्रोजनीकृत वनस्पति तेलों, पेय पदार्थों, कन्फेक्शनरी बिस्कुट और अन्य गैर-औषधीय उत्पादों का निर्माता, जहां इन 
उत्पादों को संसाधित करने के लिए ऐसी थोक औषधों की आवश्यकता होती है। 

अनुज्ञप्तिधारी अनुज्ञप्ति के तहत काम करने वाली फर्म के गठन में किसी भी बदलाव की स्थिति में अनुज्ञप्ति प्राधिकारी 
को लिखित रूप में सूचित करेगा। जहां फर्म के गठन में कोई बदलाव होता है, वहां वर्तमान अनुज्ञप्ति उस तारीख से

MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 13th November, 2026 


S.O. 6212(E).— In exercise of powers conferred by sub-section (1) of section 3A of the National Highways 
Act, 1956 (48 of 1956) (hereinafter referred to as the said Act), the Central Government, after being satisfied that for 
the public purpose, the land, the brief description of which is given in the Schedule below, is required for building 
(widening/two lane with paved shoulder/four laning etc.,), maintenance, management and operation of NH119D in the 
stretch of land from Km. 55 to Km. 109.3 (Jehanabad Bihar) in the district of JEHANABAD in the state of BIHAR, 
hereby declares its intention to acquire such land. 


Any person interested in the said land may, within twenty-one days from the date of publication of this 
notification in the Official Gazette, object to the use of such land for the aforesaid purpose under sub-section(1) of 
section 3C of the said Act. 


Every such objection shall be made to the Competent Authority, namely, DLAO Jehanabad in writing and shall 
set out the grounds thereof and the Competent Authority shall give the objector an opportunity of being heard, either in 
person or by a legal practitioner, and may, after hearing all such objections and after making such further enquiry, if 
any, as the Competent Authority thinks necessary, by order, either allow or disallow the objections. 


Any order made by the Competent Authority under sub-section (2) of section 3C of the said Act shall be final. 


The land plans and other details of the land to be acquired under their notification are available and can be

NOTIFICATION UNDER SECTION 20E OF THE RAILWAY ACT, 1989 
Bilaspur, the 16th November, 2026 


9.0. 6234(E).— Whereas, by the notification of the Government of India, In the Ministry of 
Railways (South East Central Railway) number S.O. 2146(E), dated the 30 April 2026, published in the Gazette of 
India (Extra-Ordinary) Part-II section 3 sub section (ii), (herein after referred to as the said notification) under 
subsection (1) of 20A of the Railway act,1989 (24 of 1989) (herein after referred to as the said Act), the Central 
Government declared its intention to acquire the land specified in the schedule annexed to the said notification for the 
purpose of execution of Special Railway Project, namely “Kharsia-Naya Raipur-Parmalkasa 5" and 6" line 
(278.00 km.) of South East Central Railway” the state of Chhattisgarh. 


And, whereas the substance of the said notification no. 2073 dated 30" April 2026 was published as per 
section 20A sub section (4) in the daily Newspapers, Dainik Bhaskar (Hindi) Raipur Edition dated 24.05.2026, 
Haribhoomi (Hindi) Raipur Edition dated 24.05.2026 and The Hitavada (English) Raipur Edition dated 24.05.2026. 


And whereas, objections were received within the set time period and disposed off by the Competent 
Authority under section 20D of the said Act; 


And, whereas, in pursuance of sub-section (1) of section 20E of the said act, the Competent Authority has 
submitted his report to the central Government; 


Now, therefore, upon receipt of the said report of the Competent Authority, and in exercise of the powers 
conferred by sub-section (1) of the section 20E of the said act 1989, the Central Government hereby declares that the 
land specified in the schedule annexed hereto shall be acquired for the aforesaid purpose;

MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS

NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 3th November, 2026 


99.0. 6248(E).— In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (.) of section 20A of the Railways Act, 
989 (24 of 989) (hereinafter referred to as the said Act), the Central Government, after being satisfied that for the 
public purpose, the land, the brief description of which has given in the schedule annexed hereto, is required for the 
purpose of execution, maintenance, management and operation of the Special Railway Project namely, “Construction 
of 3rd & 4th Line between Ghaziabad—Moradabad, Moradabad-Roza and Roza-Sitapur (402.78 km)” in the 
district of Moradabad in the State of Uttar Pradesh, hereby declares its intention to acquire such land; 


Any person interested in the said land may within a period of thirty days from the date of publication of this 
notification in the official Gazette, raise objection to the acquisition and use of such land for the aforesaid purpose under 
sub-section (.) of section 20 D of the said Act; 


Every such objection shall be made to the Competent Authority, namely, Special Land Acquisition Officer, 
Moradabad in writing and shall set out the grounds thereof and the Competent Authority shall give the objector an 
opportunity of being heard, either in person or by legal practitioner and may, after hearing all such objections and after 
making such further enquiry, if any, as the Competent Authority thinks necessary, by order, either allow or disallow the 
objections; 


Any order made by the Competent Authority under sub-section (2) of section 20 D of the said Act shall be 
final; 


The land plans and other details of the land covered under this notification are available and can be inspected 
by the interested person at the aforesaid office of the Competent Authority.

नियंत्रक एवं महालेखापरीक्षक , संघ लोक सेवा आयोग , आयुष मंत्रालय के सभी सम्बद्ध / अधीनस्थ कार्यालय / सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र के उपक्रम आदि 
तथा भारत सरकार के सभी मंत्रालयों / विभागों और राज्य सरकारों एवं संघ राज्य प्रशासनों को भेजी जाए । 

यह भी आदेश दिया जाता है कि संकल्प को सामान्य जानकारी के लिए भारत सरकार के राजपत्र में प्रकाशित किया जाए ।

Functions of the Samiti : 

The functions of the Samiti are to render advice regarding implementation of the provisions relating to Official 
Language contained in the Constitution , Official Languages Act and Rules , Policy decisions of the Kendriya Hindi Samiti , 
instructions issued by the Ministry of Home Affairs / Department of Official Language relating to Official Language Hindi 
and also the progressive use of Hindi in the Ministry of Ayush .

Tenure :

( b ) 


The tenure of the Samiti shall be generally three years from the date of its constitution , provided that : 

( a ) 

A member , who is a Member of Parliament , ceases to be a member of the Samiti as soon as he / she ceases to 
be a Member of Parliament . 


Ex - officio members of the Samiti shall continue as members as long as they hold the office by virtue of which 
they are members of the Samiti . 


[ PART I - SEC . 1 


( c ) 

If a vacancy arises in the Samiti due to the death , resignation etc. of any member , the member appointed 
against the vacancy shall hold office for the residual term of three years . 


Travelling and daily allowance : 


The non - official members will be paid travelling allowance by shorter route from their residence to the 
meeting as per their entitlement . They will also be paid daily allowance on rates fixed by the Government of India from time 
to time .
